author: Unknown
title: Women in Batman: The mechanism that covers up femicide must be dismantled
content:
The

I Need Peace Women’s Initiative

 held a statement outside Batman (Êlih) Bar Association for Rojwelat Kızmaz and other women killed as a result of a male-dominated mentality. A banner reading, “What happened to Rojwelat Kızmaz? Femicides must be investigated, perpetrators must be prosecuted,” was displayed.


The Turkish text of the statement was read by Yağmur Alaz Gülveren, a member of the initiative, while the Kurdish text was read by Hava Can, a member of TJA.


What happened to Rojwelat Kızmaz


Drawing attention to the relationship between violence against women and war policies, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren stated that the use of sexual violence as a weapon in wars creates conditions that allow systematic crimes against women to be covered up.


Pointing to the recording of women’s deaths in the region as “suspicious deaths,” Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said: “From a city with a deep memory of violence against women and femicides, and where such violence occurs most frequently as a result of violence by the male-dominated state, in other words, from Batman, we ask: What happened to Rojwelat Kızmaz?”


Why are the suspects not being arrested


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren also raised the case of Ipek Er, who was driven to suicide after being subjected to sexual assault by specialist sergeant Musa Orhan, and criticized the fact that the suspect had not been arrested.


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren asked: “Why has Musa Orhan still not been arrested? Do the inspection reports of the Ministry of Family and Social Services contain any warnings or administrative sanctions against the Private Şifa Care Center?”


Stating that the facts behind the classification of women’s deaths as “suicides” must be brought to light, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said, “Will the real causes of these deaths and the perpetrators be uncovered? For a genuine and lasting peace, will crimes against women be confronted, and will the perpetrators be prosecuted?”


Allegations concerning the Şifa care center


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren stated that male state violence is not limited to femicides and also drew attention to allegations concerning the Private Batman Şifa Care Center.


She said that allegations that a woman at the care center was subjected to systematic sexual assault and underwent two abortions, that people under the center’s care were subjected to torture and mistreatment, and that efforts were made to cover up suspicious deaths must be investigated.


Impunity continues


Drawing attention to a mechanism of impunity in Batman extending from deaths recorded as “female suicides” since the 1990s to femicides in which the perpetrators are known, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren stated that this was not merely a matter of isolated acts of male violence.


Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said: “This is not simply the violence of individual men; it is the organized form of male dominance, nourished by the politics of war, spreading across the entire region.”


Stating that Turkey’s security-oriented policies toward the Kurdish issue have a long history, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said that the strengthening of security policies after 2015 “combined special war policies with male dominance and hostility toward women, thereby intensifying forms of violence against women.”


We will continue our struggle for justice


Stating that they would continue their struggle for women’s right to life and freedom, Yağmur Alaz Gülveren said they would continue to follow cases that authorities seek to cover up. Yağmur Alaz Gülveren added: “For genuine peace and for women’s freedom, we say an end to special war policies and male state violence.”


The statement ended with applause and chants including “Long live women’s solidarity,” “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (“Women, Life, Freedom”), “Women do not want war, they want peace,” and “Femicide is political.”

author: Unknown
title: KNK: We will fulfill Mehdi Zana’s aspirations
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a condolence message following the death of Mehdi Zana, the former mayor of Amed.


The KNK’s message reads as follows:


“We learned with great pain and sorrow of the death of politician, writer, and former Amed Mayor Mehdi Zana. We are deeply saddened by this news. Mr. Mehdi Zana was involved in patriotic work and politics in Bakurê Kurdistan, in Amed, and throughout Kurdistan. He held a prominent position within Kurdish political circles and parties. He served as mayor of Amed between 1977 and 1980.


Because of his patriotic work and stance, he became a target of the fascist regime during the period of the September 12 military coup. He was removed from his position as mayor of Amed, arrested, and subjected to severe torture. He spent long periods in the prisons of Amed, Aydın, Afyon, and Eskişehir. In total, he spent 16 years of his life in prison.


After his release from prison, he was forced to live in Europe due to the repression and attacks by the Turkish state. In Europe, too, he continued his struggle against the occupiers and took his place in the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom. Mr. Mehdi Zana also held an important position in efforts toward national unity. He did not recognize the artificial borders and supported the revolutions in Rojhilat, Başûr, and Rojava.


We are deeply saddened by the death of Mehdi Zana and share the grief of his family and friends. On this occasion, we extend our condolences to the people of Kurdistan, the workers of the revolution, and his family. Brother Mehdi, do not worry; we will follow in your footsteps and fulfill your aspirations and your wishes.”

author: Unknown
title: Gökalp: The commune is the key to living together - Part One
content:
Suat Gökalp, who spent 33 years of his life in prison, began working to contribute to Abdullah Öcalan’s call for peace and a democratic society and his paradigm of communal society soon after regaining his freedom. Despite spending so many years under conditions of isolation, Gökalp speaks with a determination and clarity that leave little trace of the despair or anxiety often encountered outside prison. Drawing on his own life story, he spoke to ANF about conditions of isolation in prisons, the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the paradigm of communal society.


I grew up where the memory of resistance was kept alive


Suat Gökalp, 55, who describes himself as “a member of the Apo Movement,” said he has been involved in the Kurdish revolutionary struggle for 37 years. He joined the guerrillas at the age of 19 and was arrested in Istanbul in 1993, spending a total of 33 years in prison. Gökalp said he grew up in a highly politically conscious environment in central Ağrı. He said: “Ağrı itself represents an important current within the Kurdish struggle because of its history of resistance. I grew up in an environment where the memory of the Ağrı Rebellion and the resistance against the Zîlan massacre was kept alive. I spent my childhood in the Teyyare neighbourhood, which had a strong Kurdish and left-wing political consciousness, and that had a profound influence on my decision to join the struggle.”


The Kurdish people’s struggle and organised prison life kept me going


Gökalp said he left high school at the age of 19 to join the Kurdish freedom struggle. He said: “It was the 1990s, the period of the serhildan uprisings, and at the time, those who did not join the struggle were looked down upon and called opportunists. That sociopolitical climate also influenced our decision to join. People were joining in groups, one after another, during that period.” Gökalp joined the ranks of the Kurdish freedom movement without informing his family. After spending two years with the guerrillas, he was arrested in Istanbul in 1993, marking the beginning of 33 years of imprisonment. His years in prison took him through Sağmalcılar, Bayrampaşa, Ümraniye, Bursa, Kandıra and Bolu, much of that time marked by transfers and isolation. Gökalp said the sources that kept his ideological, philosophical and spiritual motivation alive in prison were both the struggle waged by the Kurdish people outside and the organised collective life maintained by prisoners. He explained that every moment of prison life was organised through collective activities, education and efforts to follow developments in the broader struggle and respond accordingly. Although physically imprisoned, he said, this allowed them to feel free in spirit.


F-Type prisons are like laboratories


Gökalp spent 18 of his 33 years of imprisonment under isolation conditions in F-Type prisons. He said: “We were the first group from our movement to be transferred to F-Type prisons. Together with our comrade Sabri Ok, 14 of us were transferred from Bursa to Kandıra F-Type Prison. I remained in F-Type prisons from late 2003 until October 2025.” Gökalp said the reality of isolation could never be fully understood without experiencing it first-hand: “We had previously read and studied how F-Type prisons were modelled on a policy used in Germany against the Red Army Faction (RAF) guerrillas. But there is a profound difference between reading about something, acquiring knowledge of it, and actually living through it. What we saw in F-Type prisons was an architecture designed to destroy the social and spiritual dimensions of a human being. From the soundproofing and the isolation of communication between cells to the paint that was used and the guards speaking exclusively in commands, we saw a prison system that had been deliberately designed down to the smallest detail. Resisting all of this required an organised, planned and disciplined stance. For us, resistance did not simply mean resisting physical attacks and torture. Resistance also meant preserving the social and spiritual dimensions of ourselves through the way we lived, while safeguarding our sociopolitical goals, our beliefs, our decisions and our motivation. Because ideology, too, is dynamic. Contrary to what people may think, it is not static. To use a metaphor, ideology is like a flower. If you water it, it stays alive; if you do not, it withers. If you do not renew and develop your ideological education every …

author: DebConf 26
title: Abstraction Leaks: Why Understanding Linux Internals Still Matters
content:
by Valentin Torassa Colombero


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/75-abstraction-leaks-why-understanding-linux-internals-still-matters/


Modern software engineering heavily relies on abstractions: containers, cloud platforms, frameworks, and managed services. While these abstractions accelerate development, they often hide the underlying complexity of the system. This talk explores what happens when those abstractions break — and why understanding Linux internals becomes essential.


This session is aimed at developers, DevOps engineers, and newcomers to Debian who want to deepen their understanding of how systems actually work. Using real-world examples from networking, process management, and resource handling, we will explore how abstraction leaks manifest in production environments.


Attendees will leave with a clearer mental model of Linux systems, an appreciation for Debian’s philosophy of transparency and control, and practical insights on how to debug, reason about, and design more resilient systems by understanding what lies beneath the abstraction layers.

title: The femicide of Sultan Kara: Special warfare and impunity together
content:
Despite requests for a restraining order and protection, no measures were taken to protect Sultan Kara, who was killed by Ersan Akdemir, from whom she was in the process of divorcing. The perpetrator was arrested, while the child who witnessed the incident was taken into state care. Drawing attention to the story behind the incident, TJA activist Bahar Peker said the killing was deliberately planned and that the perpetrator had been emboldened by impunity.


Tevgera Jinên Azad (TJA) activist Bahar Peker said that two women had been killed in Amed within the past 10 days, adding that the women’s movement had been discussing how to respond to and organize against femicides. Drawing attention to Sultan Kara, who was killed two days ago by Ersan Akdemir, from whom she was in the process of divorcing, Peker said: “Sultan Kara was killed while holding her three-year-old daughter in her arms. Kara’s family told us that Sultan had previously gone to the police and reported the problems she was experiencing, but no protective measures were taken.”


Sultan Kaya was not protected despite her complaints


Relaying the family’s account of the violence Sultan Kara had previously experienced, Peker said: “Sultan’s family told us that, before they reached the point of divorce, she had repeatedly been subjected to violence by her husband, that her teeth had been broken, and that at one point he had even tried to strangle her and, at another point, tried to stab her. Sultan was subjected to systematic violence for a long time; she lived with violence for a total of four years. In response to her family’s warnings, she said, ‘If I have a child, he will change,’ but the violence continued even during her pregnancy.”


Sultan Kaya wanted to build a new life


According to the family’s account, Peker said Sultan Kara did not want to tell her family, particularly her brother, about the violence she was experiencing. Regarding the day of the killing, she said: “After she left the house for the final time, the death threats increased even further, and he also threatened her sister. On the final day, he called her over under a pretext and deliberately killed the woman in a completely planned and calculated manner.”


Peker expressed her hope that Sultan Kara’s killing would be the last femicide in Amed and described violence against women as “part of special warfare policies,” adding: “They also told us that the man who killed Sultan Kara, her former husband, used substances. The perpetrator killed Sultan while she was holding her three-year-old daughter and then fled with the child. This is truly unacceptable. During this process, we also learned that Sultan had taken measures to defend herself against the perpetrator and the threats she was facing. She resisted until the very end for herself and her daughter; she wanted to be happy by building a new life. Despite all these calls for protection and complaints, she could not be protected.”


The policy of impunity gives men strength 


Peker said that femicides and violence against women had recently increased in Amed and stressed that perpetrators must be punished. Peker said: “As women, we now seriously demand that severe punishments be imposed on men who commit violence, on the patriarchal male mentality, on the male mindset, and on the male mindset that murders women. What is happening at this point feeds into itself. There is a serious policy of impunity. This policy of impunity strengthens and emboldens other men and the patriarchal male mentality. Behind both femicides and the increasing number of suspicious deaths, we consistently see similar stories. The stories are the same, the ending is the same, and nothing changes. A struggle must be waged to change this.”


Sultan's family demands justice


Stating that women would follow the case closely, Peker said; “As women’s organizations—as all of Amed’s women’s institutions and women’s structures—we will follow this case. At the same time, we will follow the case and the proceedings to ensure that this patriarchal male mentality receives serious punishment. We will always expand and strengthen our struggle. The family’s only demand at this point is that this person receives an aggravated life sentence.


The family says that Sultan could not be protected despite the restraining order they had requested. Unfortunately, we see this situation everywhere as femicides increase. Women are not protected when they should be; they are sent back …

title: Our history is an expression of our resistance
content:
Throughout history, Kurds have been known in each period through a hero, and that hero has left their mark on the history of resistance. In the 21st century, too, the identity of heroism that has developed under the leadership of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] is once again taking its place on the stage of history. The heroes of this century are Leader Apo and the Kurdistan guerrillas.


As is known, commemorations are being held in Northern Kurdistan for the martyrs of the Freedom Movement. Thousands of people gather around their martyrs and bid them farewell. Of course, this is not merely a commemoration; these gatherings are also an expression of the struggle waged for many years. If the martyrs of the Kurdish cause can today be received with ease, this is thanks to the efforts and resistance of our heroes. They are followers of Leader Apo and the struggle for freedom.


Looking back a few years, we can remember how our families received the bodies of their children. Because of policies of denial, annihilation, and isolation, our martyrs were delivered to their families in coffins, cargo boxes, and bags, or were not delivered at all.


There were times when even the name of Kurdishness was banned throughout Turkey, and when even uttering it was considered forbidden. A person who spoke the name of Kurdishness had to say it in a whisper. Our martyrs were commemorated amid hardship and resistance. But today, we witness how magnificently our martyrs are received in Northern Kurdistan and in cities across Turkey. The heroes of Kurdistan are commemorated with the slogans “Bê Serok Jiyan Nabe” (“There can be no life without a leader”) and “Şehit Namirin” (“Martyrs never die”).


This is the result of the efforts of the Peace and Democratic Society Process pursued by Leader Apo. We must recognize these realities clearly and approach them accordingly. If it were not for Leader Apo’s efforts and the resistance of the guerrillas, it would not have been possible for our martyrs to be received in such a magnificent manner.


As two years have passed since Leader Apo put forward his project, those who do not want social peace to emerge are disturbed by it. Time and again, they try to undermine Leader Apo’s project with meaningless statements.


However, Leader Apo stands against the provocateurs with his persistence, strength, and free will. During the commemorations of the martyrs, they may also seek to do certain things and attempt to distort the reality of our resistance. But our people must be vigilant in the face of such attempts. Because we have a very great history of resistance. The resistance experienced throughout our history has never been experienced in this way in the history of any other people. Of course, we do not belittle the resistance of other peoples; but no one has resisted to the extent that the Kurdish people have.


This is because our people have been subjected to annihilation in every sense, and every power that came to the lands of Kurdistan sought to eliminate the Kurdish people. Therefore, as we stand on the threshold of recognition of our identity, we must embrace these historic days in every possible way.


The strong will of the people of Amed comes from the resistance in prison


The city of Amed has also played a major role in and made great contributions to the resistance. Just as the flag of resistance and freedom was carried from Şêx Seîd to Nûman and Delal, today it continues to be carried in the same spirit. Amed is one of the cities of Kurdistan that has opened its doors to its revolutionary sons and daughters since 1978. The PKK’s first congress was held in Amed.


One of the first acts of resistance to leave its mark on history was the resistance in Amed Prison. This is why we say that Amed and its people are one of the arteries of the Kurdish revolution. Comrades Kemal, Mehmet Hayri, Akif, Necmi, and all the other resistance fighters of Amed Prison left the mark of their struggle on Amed. The foundation of the strong will possessed by the people of Amed today comes from the resistance in the prison. In other words, its pioneers are Mazlum Doğan, Rahşan, Çiyager, and Nûcan. Sur has its legacy of the struggle for self-governance, while Lice has its legacy of building the Freedom Movement.


With the stance of these cities, Zilan, Armanc, Agir, and their comrades have today left their mark on the struggle for heroism. Our history includes mothers and fathers who sacrificed their precious …

author: Unknown
title: Film festivals increasingly cater to the urban middle class
content:
Film festivals are held every year across all four parts of Kurdistan. The Amed Film Festival, held again this year in Diyarbakır (Amed), is one of the best known. Admission is free. Yet a large section of society remains absent from these crowds: women living in rural areas and those in the city’s informal settlements and poor neighbourhoods. The festival may be “open to everyone and free of charge,” but for these women, the door remains effectively closed. This suggests that money is not the real barrier. Even when cost is removed entirely, there is a broader social structure that still prevents women from reaching the cinema. This reality did not emerge overnight. The village evacuations and forced displacement of the 1990s uprooted families from their land and pushed them to the outskirts of cities, creating a common historical root for the two groups now described as the “rural population” and the “urban poor.”


Why, then, are women from rural areas and poor urban neighbourhoods not attending? The answer is clear: the barrier is not money, but women’s lack of time, access to transport and safety at night. In villages, a woman’s day is spent working in the fields or tending to animals; in informal settlements, housework and childcare are often compounded by informal employment. There is simply no space in her day to say, “I’m free today, I can go.” There is no childcare, and often no one else to look after the children. If screenings take place in the evening, travelling alone at night presents another safety concern. Even if a woman makes it as far as the festival door, she must first overcome three overlapping barriers: time, childcare and transport. Across both rural Kurdistan and the poorer districts of its cities, economic conditions continue to structure women’s time and mobility around the family, and often around men. Behind the question of time lies an even deeper constraint: the social disapproval women face for travelling alone into the city, going out at night or entering crowded public spaces.


Women who cannot find themselves on screen


Even if a woman overcomes all these barriers and makes it into the cinema, one question remains: does she see herself on screen? The everyday lives and labour of women in rural areas and informal settlements are rarely portrayed. In Kurdish films, female characters are often written by male directors; women tend to be depicted either through their suffering or as bearers of tradition. This is no coincidence. It is a consequence of how filmmaking itself is structured: who gets to make films, whose projects receive funding and which directors are given visibility. From the outset, this system leaves women from rural communities and poor urban neighbourhoods outside the frame.


Another language


There is yet another barrier: language. Festival programmes are largely conducted in Turkish. For rural women who speak no language other than Kurdish and have had limited access to formal education, this creates an additional layer of exclusion. A woman who has grown up speaking her own language is forced to watch even her own story through another language. Eventually, she comes to see cinema as something that “does not belong to me,” while cinema continues to tell her story in her absence. For these women, television has become the only screen available at home. For those unable to reach a cinema, their relationship with moving images is almost entirely confined to television. Yet television reproduces the same problem: series and programmes portray an urban, middle-class way of life, once again pushing women from rural communities and informal settlements to the margins. Whether at the cinema or in front of the television at home, women do not see their own stories reflected at them. Whichever screen they look at, the life they see is always someone else’s.


Geared towards middle- and upper-income audiences


This is not unique to Diyarbakır. The Amed Film Festival is one of the region’s longest-established cultural events, but it has always been held in the city centre, effectively excluding women in villages and informal settlements from the outset. In Southern Kurdistan (Başur), the Duhok International Film Festival has become a well-known event, but its reach has not extended to villages and poor neighbourhoods to the same extent. The festival is increasingly geared towards an urban, educated, middle and upper income audience.

title: University of Rojava denounces restrictions on Kurdish, calls for a bilingual education model
content:
The University of Rojava in Qamishlo issued a statement regarding the recent decisions taken by the Syrian Ministry of Education, stating the following:


“The University of Rojava emphasizes that the right to receive education in one’s mother tongue across various fields of science and knowledge is an academic and human right guaranteed by international standards and conventions.


The University of Rojava is closely following the recent decisions taken by the Syrian Ministry of Education, including the reduction of Kurdish-language classes to three periods per week. Based on its academic and educational assessments, the university stresses that this measure represents a departure from the established educational model and constitutes a regressive step that undermines the continuous progress made in the region’s education system over the past years.


Over the past 12 years, Rojava/North and East Syria has accumulated extensive scientific and practical experience in building a comprehensive education system in which Kurdish has been established as a primary language of instruction and research at all levels of education. The use of the mother tongue has not been limited to departments of literature and the humanities; courses in all basic, medical, and applied sciences—including mathematics, physics, chemistry, and engineering—have also been taught in Kurdish in accordance with advanced scientific curricula and academic standards.


Restricting and separating the language of instruction to three classes per week, and reducing it to the status of a secondary language course rather than using it as a primary medium for teaching scientific subjects, entails the following negative educational and academic consequences:


The weakening of students’ comprehension and analytical abilities as a result of being disconnected from the linguistic environment in which they have received sustained academic investment for more than 12 years.


The abandonment of the educational infrastructure and academic achievements that have been built and developed through 12 years of sustained effort and investment in educational resources.


The disregard of international educational standards and conventions that emphasize mother-tongue education as a fundamental factor in ensuring the quality of education and fostering innovation and critical thinking.


To set the course of education on the right path, the university emphasizes that the best academic solution lies not in restricting one language at the expense of another, but in adopting a bilingual education model. This is a model implemented at both scientific and global levels, allowing core sciences and subjects to be taught side by side in both Kurdish and Arabic. In this way, students’ linguistic and cultural rights are safeguarded, their scientific and communicative capacities are enhanced, and a bridge of academic and national integration is built in place of policies of exclusion and restriction.


The University of Rojava emphasizes that the right to receive education in one’s mother tongue across different fields of science is an academic and human right protected by international standards and conventions, and that it is an essential means of ensuring the stability of the educational process and advancing scientific research. Furthermore, rather than implementing policies of restriction and reduction, multilingualism should be strengthened and inclusive educational curricula adopted in order to build an inclusive and sustainable education system.


On this basis, the University of Rojava calls on the relevant parties to reconsider the decision restricting Kurdish-language education. In order to safeguard the future of generations of students and preserve the quality of the education system, the university stresses the need to work toward maintaining and further developing the academic standards and comprehensive scientific curricula that have been taught in Kurdish over the past 12 years, while also paving the way for the development of sustainable bilingual education models.”

title: Rafael Leao'nun maliyeti açıklandı
content:
Galatasaray, Rafael Leao transferi için İtalyan ekibi Milan ile anlaşmaya varıldığını duyurdu. Sarı-kırmızılılar, Leao için 38 milyon avro bonservis bedeli ödeyecek. 4 yıllık sözleşme imzalayan 27 yaşındaki futbolcu, yıllık 10 milyon Euro garanti ücret kazanacak.

Sarı-kırmızılılardan yapılan açıklama şu şekilde:

"Profesyonel futbolcu Rafael Alexandre Da Conceição Leão’nun transferi konusunda, oyuncunun kulübü AC Milan S.p.A. ile anlaşmaya varılmıştır.

Bu kapsamda, futbolcunun kulübüne toplam 38.000.000 avro tutarında sabit transfer bedeli ödenecektir. Ayrıca, futbolcunun bir sonraki satışından elde edilecek kârın %20’lik bölümü AC Milan S.p.A.’ya ödenecektir.

Futbolcu ile 2026-2027 sezonundan itibaren geçerli olmak üzere 4 yıllık sözleşme imzalanmıştır. Yapılan anlaşmaya göre futbolcuya her bir sezon için net 10.000.000 avro garanti ücret ödenecektir."

Galatasaray, bu yaz transfer döneminde Fransız Lesley Ugochukwu ve Rus Aleksey Batrakov'un ardından İtalya ekibi Milan'dan 38 milyon avro bonservis bedeli karşılığında 27 yaşındaki kanat oyuncusu Rafael Leao'yu kadrosuna kattı. Leao, böylece Galatasaray tarihindeki 7. Portekizli oyuncu oldu.

content:
Samsun’da 30 Ağustos Zafer Bayramı'nın 104'üncü yıl dönümü kutlamaları çerçevesinde resmi törenlerin ardından alternatif program gerçekleştirildi. Valilik tarafından düzenlenen resmi geçit töreninin ardından KESK, DİSK, TMMOB, Samsun Barosu ve meslek odaları ile siyasi partiler Atatürk Anıtı’na çelenk bırakarak saygı duruşunda bulundu.

Törende konuşan Yeni Parti Samsun İl Başkanı Mehmet Özdağ, milli mücadelenin ilk adımının atıldığı Samsun'da 30 Ağustos coşkusunu paylaşmaktan gurur duyduklarını belirtti.

30 Ağustos Zafer Bayramı'nın partileri açısından tarihi bir öneme sahip olduğunu aktaran Mehmet Özdağ, "Bu yıl bizim için ayrı bir anlam taşıyor. Çünkü bu, Yeni Parti olarak kutladığımız ilk resmi bayramımız. Milletimiz ülkemizin aydınlık geleceğini yeniden inşa etmek üzere partimizi kurmuştur. Bu hareket aşağıdan yukarıya, halkın öz iradesiyle yükselmiştir" dedi.

Özdağ, "104 yıl önce nasıl bir kurtuluş mücadelesi verildiyse, bugün milletimiz bir kez daha, ceberrut, baskıcı, milletin alın terini sömüren AKP rejimine karşı, refah dolu, özgür, adil ve sosyal hukuk devleti olma yolunda yeni bir kurtuluş mücadelesi vermektedir" ifadelerini kullandı.

Yeni Parti Genel Başkan Özgür Özel’in liderliğinde Samsun'un her mahallesinde çalışma yürüteceklerini kaydeden Özdağ, "Sokak sokak, mahalle mahalle, hane hane dolaşacak, çalmadık kapı, sıkılmadık el bırakmayacağız" dedi.

Samsun topraklarında Cumhuriyet mirasına sahip çıkacaklarını belirten Özdağ, "Bağımsız, özgür, laik ve demokratik Cumhuriyet'i, adaletin, refahın ve millet egemenliğinin gerçek anlamda hakim olduğu bir Türkiye'ye taşımak, bugün hepimizin ortak sorumluluğudur" diye konuştu.

author: DebConf 26
title: Making sense of 30 million emails: Introducing the LKML5Ws Dataset
content:
by David Tadokoro


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/71-making-sense-of-30-million-emails-introducing-the-lkml5ws-dataset/


The Linux kernel uses mailing lists as the primary medium for all development, bug reporting, and pivotal discussions regarding the project's future, a practice also observed in other large Free Software projects. However, as a consequence of this decentralized development model, these emails are spread across hundreds of mailing lists, each with its own community and code-maintenance model.


This talk presents the LKML5Ws dataset ("the What, When, Who, Where, and Why in the Linux Kernel Mailing Lists"). With over 20 million emails from 345 different mailing lists, our massive relational dataset provides a comprehensive overview of the last 20 years of Linux kernel development. Beyond shedding light on the awe-inspiring number of patches, discussions, and contributors, our dataset serves as a basis for studying the intricate, knowledge-rich nature of free software development. We want to share and discuss this data, along with some visualizations, with the Debian community.

title: 'Millet Şahidimdir' kitabının yasaklanmasına Kırmızı Kedi'den tepki
content:
Silivri Cezaevi'nde tutuklu olan İBB Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu'nun savunma metinlerinden oluşan 'Millet Şahidimdir' kitabına, henüz matbaa sürecindeyken İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın başvurusuyla getirilen basım, dağıtım ve satış yasağına yönelik tepkiler sürüyor.

Eseri yayıma hazırlayan Kırmızı Kedi Yayınevi'nin sahibi Haluk Hepkon, söz konusu karara dair tepkisini dile getirdi.

Kırmızı Kedi, ilk günden beri cumhuriyeti, demokrasiyi savundu. Birçok kitabımız Türkiye'de konuşuldu, tartışıldı, gündemi belirledi. Hukuksuzluğa karşı hep mücadele ettik. Ekrem İmamoğlu'nun yazdığı "Millet Şahidimdir" 2000. kitabımızdı. Matbaada el konuldu, yasaklandı. Bu…

Yayınevinin yayın hayatı boyunca demokrasi değerlerinin arkasında durduğunu vurgulayan Hepkon, “Birçok kitabımız Türkiye'de konuşuldu, tartışıldı, gündemi belirledi. Hukuksuzluğa karşı hep mücadele ettik” dedi.

İmamoğlu'nun kaleme aldığı çalışmanın yayınevlerinin 2000. yayını olma özelliği taşıdığını ifade eden Hepkon, açıklamasını şu sözlerle sürdürdü:

“Kitabımıza matbaada el konuldu, yasaklandı. Bu hukuksuz ve zorlu süreçte yanımızda olan herkese teşekkür ediyoruz. Bu teşekkür sadece yanımızda oldukları için değil, esas olarak hukukun ve cumhuriyetin yanında oldukları için. Émile Zola'nın dediği gibi, ‘Gerçek yürüyor, onu hiçbir şey durduramaz…”

author: DebConf 26
title: Debian in Disaster + Security Incidents
content:
by Michael Prokop


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/25-debian-in-disaster-security-incidents/


In his day-to-day work, the speaker is responsible, among other things, for ensuring the stable and secure operation of Debian servers at various companies.


However, there are frequent incidents where the speaker has to step in as a firefighter, whether to deal with malfunctioning services or servers, or even hacked companies.


We'll take a look at the factors that contribute to such emergency incidents, and how they might have been prevented.


In this talk we'll also examine tools and services which help to ensure the reliable operation of Debian servers.


This talk is aimed at system administrators, forensics investigators, and anyone interested in improving the reliability of Debian-based systems.

title: Mersin'e giden feribot Girne açıklarında battı: 267 kişiyi taşıyordu
content:
KKTC sahile 4 mil açıkta Girne-Taşucu seferini yapan, Mersin'e giden 267 kişilik yolcu gemisi Girne açıklarında battı. Bayındırlık ve Ulaştırma Bakanı Erhan Arıklı, Girne açıklarındaki feribotun su aldığını, kurtarma çalışmalarına devam ettiklerini duyurdu.

Saat 12.30 sıralarında Girne Limanı'ndan Mersin'in Taşucu Limanı'na hareket eden özel firmaya ait yolcu gemisi, limandan ayrıldıktan hemen sonra henüz bilinmeyen nedenle su almaya başladı. Feribotun su almasının ardından kaptanın yardım çağrıları üzerine sahil güvenlik ve liman yönetimince bölgeye kurtarma ekipleri sevk edildi.

Bakan Erhan Arıklı, AA muhabirine yaptığı açıklamada, feribotun su aldığını belirterek, kurtarma çalışmalarına devam ettiklerini söyledi. Feribotta 259'u yolcu ve 8'i mürettebat olmak üzere 267 kişinin bulunduğu bilgisini veren Arıklı, geminin neden su aldığına ilişkin henüz bir bulguya ulaşılamadığını dile getirdi.

Görgü tanıkları, geminin su almasının ardından yolculardan bazılarının denize atladıklarını belirtti. Bölgedeki balıkçı teknelerinin de kurtarma çalışmalarına katıldıkları bildirildi.

author: DebConf 26
title: Use of local Infrastructure and free software for the practical implementation of secure and sovereign AI.
content:
by FERNANDO VILLARES


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/84-use-of-local-infrastructure-and-free-software-for-the-practical-implementation-of-secure-and-sovereign-ai/


This presentation explores the critical shift from cloud-based Artificial Intelligence to local, sovereign implementations. It addresses the technical and ethical challenges of modern AI, including the "Superalignment Paradox" and the risks of data dependency and post-truth. By analyzing the pros and cons of cloud versus local models (such as Gemma, QWEN, and DeepSeek), we advocate for technological sovereignty, especially within State infrastructures. The session concludes with a practical overview of tools like Ollama running on proxmox and debian with gpu passthrough technology and the current computing power in Argentina, demonstrating how local hardware and open-source software can ensure data privacy, security, and strategic independence.


Keywords: Local AI, Technological Sovereignty, LLM, Open Source, Cybersecurity, Superalignment.


Room: Aula Magna - FADU


Scheduled start: 2026-07-23 14:00:00-03:00

author: DebConf 26
title: You Really Want an AI Agent in the Cloud… But You Only Have Five Dollars
content:
by Esteban Monge


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/108-you-really-want-an-ai-agent-in-the-cloud-but-you-only-have-five-dollars/


Artificial Intelligence agents are often presented as something that requires expensive GPUs, paid subscriptions, and large cloud infrastructures. But what if you only have a small budget, a Debian server, and curiosity?


In this talk, I will show how I built a functional AI agent using mostly open technologies and low-cost services. The project combines Debian Project, Linode infrastructure, OpenRouter APIs, Telegram as the user interface, and Python as the glue connecting everything together.


The session will cover practical lessons learned while deploying and maintaining the bot, including hosting considerations, API costs, open-source AI models, automation, limitations of low-budget environments, and why Debian remains an excellent platform for experimentation and self-hosting.


This is not a corporate “AI strategy” presentation. It is a practical, honest, and accessible look at building useful AI systems with limited resources and open tools.


Room: Aula Magna - FADU


Scheduled start: 2026-07-23 11:00:00-03:00

author: Unknown
title: Young people, neglect and drug addiction in Diyarbakır’s districts
content:
Drug use and trafficking in Kurdistan, along with other related special warfare policies, are becoming increasingly entrenched. This is particularly evident in Diyarbakır (Amed) and its districts, where the situation reveals a process through which Kurdish young people are being disconnected from real life. Field studies conducted by the Center for Field Studies (SAMER) in the districts of Bağlar (Rêzan), Bismil, Silvan (Farqîn) and Ergani (Erxenî) shed light on the scale of drug use among young people.


Interviews with young people aged between 15 and 29 reveal that what official discourse reduces to a “public security issue” is, in fact, a present-day reflection of four decades of war, forced displacement and policies of denial. Behind the survey results lie municipal budgets depleted under government-appointed trustees, youth centres that were shut down, homes left abandoned, and an entire generation left to fend for itself on streets neglected by the state.


A common picture across four districts


In Bağlar, 63.3 percent of the 600 young people interviewed said they had tried cigarettes at least once in their lives, while 72.2 percent of those who had used substances said their first experience occurred before the age of 17. The picture is even more severe in Bismil, where 67 percent of young people are no longer attending school and 54.6 percent work without social security coverage. In some neighbourhoods, the age at which children begin using substances has fallen as low as eight or nine.


In Silvan, 83.8 percent of respondents believe substance use is widespread across the district. In the Kale neighbourhood, what is described as a “cycle of collapse”, unemployment, substance use, crime, social disintegration, isolation and a return to substance use, offers a stark picture of the reality facing the area. In Ergani, meanwhile, the divide between poorer neighbourhoods such as Şirinevler and relatively affluent areas once again exposes the class dimension of addiction.


The same findings recur across all four districts. Abandoned buildings and vacant homes have become centres of substance use, while areas around schools, such as Ulutürk Secondary School in Bismil, have turned into open drug-dealing points. Lighting in parks is systematically broken or out of service, leaving women unable to go out in the evenings.


This is no coincidental overlap. What emerges across four different districts is the same pattern of political and social neglect.


A generation growing up under the shadow of trustees


To understand this picture, it is necessary to look back at the period since 2016. The removal of democratically elected municipal co-mayors and their replacement by government-appointed trustees meant the systematic dismantling of youth policies, social services and local solidarity networks. Women’s shelters, youth centers, language and cultural courses, cooperatives and solidarity initiatives previously run by municipalities governed by the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) were largely abolished or rendered ineffective. SAMER’s findings today, including “a lack of social spaces and activities for young people,” “a loss of trust in municipalities” and “failure to meet demands for services”, should be understood as a direct consequence of the trustee administration process.


Indeed, SAMER’s report itself indirectly supports this assessment. The fact that access to the swimming pool complex in Bismil’s Dicle neighbourhood has effectively become fee-based, that investment in sanitation and playgrounds in Muradiye has been neglected for years, and that abandoned buildings across almost every neighbourhood of Bağlar have neither been demolished nor made safe can be seen as concrete indications that trustee administrations were shaped by a security-driven approach to control rather than by the needs of local communities.


Although municipalities governed by the DEM Party have begun demolishing abandoned buildings during the current period, it is still possible to say that structural steps have yet to be taken to address the broader problems.


The new front of special warfare: Substance use


The concept of “special warfare,” long discussed within the Kurdish political movement, is not limited to direct violence. It also encompasses indirect methods that deprive a society of its capacity to resist, organise and generate hope. The introduction of young people to drugs has historically been …

author: Unknown
title: Hollanda'da kırmızı alarm: Trump figürüyle piyasaya sürülen ekstazi haplarında ölüm tehlikesi
content:
Hollanda’da bağımlılık ve ruh sağlığı alanında çalışmalar yürüten Trimbos Enstitüsü, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump’ın başı şeklindeki ekstazi hapları nedeniyle ülke genelinde “kırmızı alarm” verdi.

T24’ün haberine göre, uyuşturucu test merkezlerine getirilen haplarda çok yüksek miktarda PMMA tespit edildiği bildirildi. Hollanda Adli Tıp Enstitüsünün de benzer bir hapı incelediği belirtildi.

Enstitü, söz konusu hapların hiçbir koşulda kullanılmaması gerektiğini vurguladı.

Farklı renklerde üretildiği belirlenen hapların ön yüzünde Trump’ın başını andıran bir figür bulunuyor. Arka yüzlerinde ise bölme çizgisinin iki tarafına yerleştirilen “NL” ve “Trump” ifadeleri yer alıyor.

PMMA, ekstazinin etkin maddesi MDMA’ya benzeyen sentetik bir madde olarak biliniyor. Ancak PMMA’nın etkisi daha geç ortaya çıkıyor ve uyarıcı etkisi daha zayıf hissedilebiliyor.

Bu nedenle kullanıcıların hapın etkisini göstermediğini düşünerek daha fazla miktarda tüketebileceği ve aşırı doz riskinin artabileceğine dikkat çekildi.

Uzmanlar, PMMA içeren hapların kullanılmasından saatler sonra mide bulantısı, kalp atışında hızlanma, nöbet ve vücut sıcaklığında tehlikeli yükselme görülebileceğini bildirdi.

Vücut sıcaklığındaki aşırı artışın ölümcül sonuçlara yol açabileceği uyarısı yapılırken ciddi belirtiler gösteren kişiler için derhal sağlık ekiplerinden yardım istenmesi gerektiği kaydedildi.

Trimbos Enstitüsü Sözcüsü Anniek Groothuis, şu ana kadar söz konusu haplarla bağlantılı herhangi bir ölüm veya ciddi sağlık vakasının kendilerine bildirilmediğini açıkladı.

Trump’ın yüzü şeklindeki ekstazi hapları daha önce de Avrupa’da ortaya çıkmıştı. Alman polisi, 2017 yılında yaklaşık 5 bin turuncu Trump figürlü ekstazi hapına el koymuştu.

Hapların internette, Trump’ın seçim sloganından uyarlanan “Trump makes partying great again” ifadesiyle pazarlandığı öne sürülmüştü.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 30 août
content:
Aujourd'hui 30 août, l'éphéméride des luttes saborde le vieux monde et cherche à l'envoyer par le fond. Et notamment ceux qui le défendent, que ce soient les sièges de la police, de la pénitentiaire ou des grands industriels.


1957 :

 A Barcelone, en pleine dictatute franquiste, mort du guérillero anarchiste José Lluís Facerías sous les balles de la police.


1970 :

 "Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid" revendique l'explosion du domicile du chef de la police métropolitaine de Londres.


1971 :

 A San Francisco et Sacramento, le Weather Underground fait sauter des bureaux de la direction de l'administration pénitentiaire suite à l'assassinat en prison du militant des Black Panthers George Jackson 9 jours plus tôt.


1974 :

 - A Tokyo, l'armée rouge japonaise fait exploser une énorme bombe au siège principal de Mitsubishi, faisant de gros dégâts.


 A Paris, une 4L bourrée d'exposifs saute devant les locaux du journal fasciste 'Minute', revendiqué en soutien à la lutte en Palestine. Les enquêtes redirigeront l'affaire vers Carlos.


1977 :

 A Rome, le cinéma 'Ariston' est incendié, alors qu'il avait dans sa programmation un film sur 'Entebbe', à savoir l'intervention des forces armées israéliennes contre le détournement d'un avion par un commando mixte du FPLP et des

Cellules Révolutionnaires

 allemandes.


1988 :

 En Irlande du Nord, trois militants de l'IRA (Gerard et Martin Harte, et Brain Mullin) sont abattus par les forces armées britanniques.


2007 :

 En Norvège, un navire de la flotte de chasse à la baleine est coulé par un groupe qui pénètre dans le bateau et ouvre les valves d'eau à l'intérieur. Plus de deux millions d'euros de dégâts. C'est le cinquième navire baleinier norvégien qui est coulé depuis 1992. Action revendiquée 'Agenda 21'.


2010 :

 A Minsk en Biélorussie, un groupe anarchiste attaque une ambassade russe au molotov et incendie des voitures officielles en solidarité avec la lutte pour la défense de la forêt de Khimki en banlieue de Moscou.


2013 :

 A Bussoleno en Italie, deux compresseurs de l'entreprise Geomont sont incendiés dans la nuit, dans le cadre de la lutte No TAV contre la construction de la ligne de TGV Lyon-Turin.


2016 :

 A Bruges, un pont en construction sur l'autoroute A11, nouveau tronçon qui doit relier Knokke à Bruges a été incendié et a entièrement brûlé.

Les travaux sont effectués par des entreprises qui, à part construire des autoroutes pour améliorer les flux de l'économie capitaliste, construisent aussi des prisons pour défendre l'État, sa loi et la propriété privée. Il s'agit de DG Infra+ (constructeur de la nouvelle prison de Marche-en-Famenne) et Willemen (construction de la nouvelle prison de Leuze-en-Hainaut).

 (

La Cavale

 via

Cette Semaine

).

 du 30 août pour plus de biographies.

title: Melih Gökçek'ten hakkında açılan soruşturmaya ilişkin açıklama: Gerekli bilgileri savcılığa vereceğim
content:
Eski Ankara Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı İbrahim Melih Gökçek ve ailesinin Avrupa'daki milyonlarca avroluk yatırımları ile kayıt dışı para transferlerinin yargıya taşınmasının ardından Melih Gökçek, açıklama yaptı.

Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın resen soruşturma başlattığını duyurmasının ardından sosyal medya hesabından açıklama yapan Gökçek, savcılığa gerekli bilgileri vereceğini söyledi.

Gökçek açıklamasında şu ifadeleri kullandı:

“Biraz önce medyaya intikal eden bilgilere göre Ankara Başsavcılığı, Murat Ağırel’in benim hakkımdaki iddialarıyla ilgili olarak maddi gerçeğin ortaya çıkarılması amacıyla resen soruşturma başlatmıştır… Allah’ın izniyle veremeyeceğim hesabım yoktur. Gerekli bilgileri savcılığa vereceğim… Kendimi Türk adaletine teslim ediyorum…”

Gazeteci Murat Ağırel Onlar TV yayını ve köşe yazısında Melih Gökçek’in yurt dışındaki mal varlığına ilişkin resmi kayıtları paylaşmıştı. Ağırel’in yazısında, Almanya merkezli finansal hareketler de yer aldı. Ağırel’in ulaştığı resmi kayıtlara göre Gökçek ailesi, Düsseldorf kentinde HAMAG Holding aracılığıyla 15 daireden oluşan bir bina satın aldı.

Alımdaki resmi bedelin 3 milyon 850 bin avro olduğu, yapılan yenileme ve tadilat çalışmalarıyla birlikte toplam harcamanın 4.5 milyon avro seviyesine ulaştığı belirtildi.

author: DebConf 26
title: De Docker monolítico a una microinfraestructura con Proxmox: un recorrido práctico
content:
by Constanza Quaglia


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/42-de-docker-monolitico-a-una-microinfraestructura-con-proxmox-un-recorrido-practico/


Esta charla presenta una migración práctica desde una infraestructura heredada de Docker hacia una arquitectura modular construida con Proxmox VE y contenedores LXC, basada en un caso real. La transición surgió de la necesidad de "rescatar" servicios críticos que funcionaban en un servidor antiguo con una versión obsoleta de Docker, sin provocar interrupciones en el servicio. Como primer paso, todo el sistema heredado fue encapsulado en un único contenedor dentro de Proxmox, preservando su funcionamiento y desacoplándolo del host original. A partir de allí, los servicios se van extrayendo y migrando progresivamente a contenedores dedicados y actualizados, permitiendo una modernización gradual y controlada.


La charla está orientada a desarrolladores, administradores de sistemas y profesionales de DevOps que se sienten cómodos trabajando con Linux y contenedores, pero que buscan alternativas más simples que Kubernetes para despliegues pequeños y medianos. Se explora cómo combinar herramientas basadas en Debian para construir una infraestructura flexible, utilizando LXC para el aislamiento, Docker para el empaquetado de aplicaciones y Traefik para el enrutamiento dinámico. Los asistentes aprenderán a diseñar sistemas que permitan migraciones incrementales manteniendo los servicios disponibles de forma continua.

author: DebConf 26
title: (Por qué|Quién|Dónde) Rust
content:
by Nicolas Antinori


by aleiton


by hernangonzalez


by tkenda


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/22-por-quequiendonde-rust/


Durante décadas, la programación de sistemas de bajo nivel ha significado elegir entre seguridad y rendimiento. A medida que estos sistemas se vuelven más complejos, el impacto de los errores de memoria y los problemas de concurrencia no para de crecer. Esta charla analiza cómo encaja Rust dentro del desarrollo open-source, particularmente dentro de los ecosistemas de Linux y Debian.


Comenzaremos con las razones por las cuales Rust está ganando terreno. Al examinar los fallos comunes de C/C++ (invalidación de iteradores, comportamiento indefinido, falta de seguridad de hilos), mostraremos cómo el borrow checker y el sistema de tipos de Rust detectan categorías enteras de errores en tiempo de compilación. También veremos cómo Rust podría haber evitado fallos del mundo real como Heartbleed.


Luego veremos quién lo está usando realmente. Rust ya está en el kernel de Linux, y organizaciones como Google, Microsoft, Canonical, Discord y Cloudflare lo utilizan en producción. Estos no son experimentos, demuestran que el lenguaje está listo para el tipo de infraestructura que mantenemos todos los días.


Finalmente, hablaremos sobre cómo involucrarse. La comunidad de Rust es activa y acogedora, y compartiremos recursos para encontrar soporte, contribuir a proyectos de Rust de código abierto y conectar con otros Rustaceans.

title: You Too Can Fix That Bug on That Weird Architecture

by Alper Nebi Yasak


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/51-you-too-can-fix-that-bug-on-that-weird-architecture/


Just before the Debian Trixie freeze, I worked on upgrading Debian’s PulseAudio package to the upstream version 17.0 for improved hardware support on devices I care about. However, it depended on a new upstream version of the WebRTC Audio Processing library, which hadn’t been updated for years in the Debian archive, and would fail to build on the mips64el architecture. Being somewhat familiar with running foreign-architecture programs through emulation for ARM systems, I decided to try fixing it without knowing anything about MIPS…


That mips64el architecture might be gone from the archive now, but Debian supports a great deal of different CPU architectures. So, this talk is about ways to build, run, test, investigate and fix foreign-architecture programs and packages on your ordinary AMD64 system, from an advanced beginner, with a real-life example. Maybe even mentions of other common problems that might come up, tricks and solutions you can use. But the main point is, architecture-specific bugs are not arcane magic that only wizards can comprehend. Probably.

Contributing to free software communities goes far beyond writing code, opening pull requests, or fixing bugs. Projects rarely fail due to technical limitations—they fail due to human burnout, poorly resolved conflicts, and relationships that break down over time.


In this talk, we will discuss the soft skills that truly sustain Free Software communities and that almost never appear in the documentation: clear communication, empathy with beginners, healthy disagreement, emotional responsibility, and consistency in collaboration.


The goal is to provoke reflection on the role of each contributor in the health of the project and present practical triggers that can be applied daily, regardless of technical level or experience.

author: DebConf 26
title: Licencia para ignorar: Por qué ya nadie lee el archivo LICENSE
content:
by Margarita Manterola


At: DebConf26


https://debconf26.debconf.org/talks/121-licencia-para-ignorar-por-que-ya-nadie-lee-el-archivo-license/


¿Alguna vez subiste un proyecto a GitHub y simplemente no pusiste licencia porque no sabías cuál elegir? ¿O elegiste MIT porque era la primera opción y sonaba simple? Es lo que hace hoy mucha gente joven que recién empieza a programar, y probablemente nadie les explicó por qué eso importa.


Puede parecer que las licencias son solo la "letra chica", aburrida, que se puede ignorar. ¡Pero no! Son el mecanismo que hace libre al software libre. Sin una licencia, ese código que subiste con tanto esfuerzo, nadie debería usarlo, modificarlo ni redistribuirlo de forma legal. Y elegir la licencia más permisiva sin pensarlo tampoco es una decisión inocente: le da ventaja a quien tenga los recursos para tomar tu trabajo, cerrarlo y sacarle provecho sin devolverte nada.


Quienes contribuimos en Debian, tenemos que lidiar con licencias todo el tiempo: al empaquetar software, al elegir cómo licenciar nuestro propio código, al revisar si algo cumple con las DFSG. Entender esto desde el principio te va a ahorrar dolores de cabeza y te va a ayudar a tomar decisiones con criterio propio, en vez de copiar lo que hace todo el mundo sin preguntarte por qué.


En esta charla vamos a explicar, sin necesidad de ser abogados, para qué sirven realmente las licencias, por qué "sin licencia" es peor que cualquier licencia, y por qué elegir entre una licencia permisiva y una copyleft es una decisión de valores, no solo un detalle técnico. Y vamos a pensar juntos qué podemos hacer, como nueva generación de contribuidores, para que esto no se siga perdiendo.

Over the past two years as Debian Project Leader, I've been involved in many parts of Debian's day-to-day work and coordination. This talk is a reflection on that experience and on how Debian functions as a do-ocracy and a global volunteer project.


I'll discuss what I set out to do, what we were able to accomplish together, and where things turned out to be more difficult than expected. The talk will look at what helps            collaboration work well in Debian, where friction can arise, and what it means to coordinate a large, diverse project without formal hierarchies.


I'll also reflect on how Debian deals with change - in technology, community dynamics, and shared understandings - while remaining grounded in its core values. While based on my time   as DPL, the focus is on the project and its structures, with the aim of sharing observations that may be useful for other long-running, volunteer-driven free software communities.

author: mini-DebConf Germany
title: Putting Past Upstream History in Debian Git
content:
by Marc Haber


At: MiniDebConf Hamburg 2026


https://hamburg2026.mini.debconf.org/talks/17-putting-past-upstream-history-in-debian-git/


Today, both Debian packaging and Upstream development happens in git, yet it is still common to pull Upstream sources into Debian by means of a release tarball. Workflows incorporating Upstream git into Debian's repositories are becoming increasingly common, but all those start with a repository that was started in the old-fashioned way, cementing the historical disconnect.


This talk explores techniques for integrating the past development history both Upstream and in Debian, creating the illusion that the repository was actually built that way from an earlier time.


Using the aide package as a case study, it demonstrates three distinct approaches: starting integration from the present, fully preserving both upstream and Debian histories, and reconstructing a unified history by replaying Debian changes on top of upstream commits.


The session analyzes the trade-offs between historical fidelity, repository readability, and maintenance complexity, and shows why preserving upstream commit identity is often more valuable than retaining Debian commit IDs. It also highlights practical challenges, including mismatches between upstream tags and release tarballs, limitations of current tooling such as git-buildpackage, and the effort required to reconcile divergent histories.

With the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) looming on the not-so-distant horizon SBOMs have emerged as the primary standard for describing the contents of your products. As none of the tools available produced adequate SBOMs for Debian-based systems we decided to roll our own:

debsbom

, which is already available for Debian and has a backport for Debian trixie.


In this talk I will talk about what SBOMs are, what makes them actually useful and what this specifically means for Debian SBOMs. I will take a dive into Debian packages and their relationships and how all of that can be modeled in an SBOM. To bring it all together I will go through common workflows and how they can now be automated with the help of debsbom.


I would also like to use this talk to open a discussion about some areas of improvement for Debian packages.

author: Unknown
title: ‘Harry Potter’ın markalaşan 25 yılı
content:
Harry Potter filminden bir sahne

Irmak Su Timur [email protected]

“Harry Potter” ilk filminin çıkması üzerinden yaklaşık 25 yıl geçmişken tekrardan dönüyor ancak bu sefer diziye uyarlanmış şekilde. Geçen bunca yılın ardından hâlâ kendinden söz ettirmeye; kitapları basılmaya, filmleri izlenmeye devam ediyor. Şimdi ise aynı hikaye bu sefer dizi olarak önümüze geliyor. Kendini büyük çoğunlukla filmleri sayesinde unutturmayan seri hakkında, başka bir gerçek de çok büyük bir marka olması… Ve bu marka yalnızca filmlerden oluşmuyor.

“Harry Potter” bir nevi kendi tüketim dünyasını da kurmuş oldu. Kitapların ve filmlerin yanında kıyafetler, oyuncaklar, koleksiyon ürünleri, oyunlar, ev eşyaları ve sayısız lisanslı ürün çıktı. Hatta tema parkı bile var. “Harry Potter”ı sevmek, yalnızca filmleri izlemek ya da kitapları okumakla sınırlı kalmadı. Bir noktadan sonra “Harry Potter” evrenini takip etmekle o dünyaya ait hissetmek arasındaki mesafe de azaldı. Bu durum tabii ki “Harry Potter”a özel değil. Büyük film ve oyun serilerinin önemli bir bölümü artık benzer şekilde çalışıyor. Ancak “Harry Potter”ın zamanla kurduğu ilişki biraz daha farklı. Çünkü seri birden fazla kuşağın çocukluğuna dokundu. İlk filmlerle büyüyenler bugün yeni dizinin hedef kitlesinin bir parçası olacak. Aynı zamanda onların çocukları da hedef kitlesinin bir parçası…

Serinin yıllarca gündemde kalmasının bir başka yanı da hikayenin hiçbir zaman tamamen tamamlanmış gibi davranmaması. Kitaplar ve filmler tamamlanmış olsa da “Harry Potter”ı konuşmaya devam eden, Yazarı J.K. Rowling’in zaman zaman seri ve karakterler hakkında verdiği yeni bilgiler gündeme gelmişti. Yazarın bugün serveti 1 milyar doları geçmişte olsa hâlâ seriyi gerektiğini düşündüğü yerlerde anlık yaptığı paylaşımlarla anmaktan geri durmuyor.

Yeni diziyi ilginç kılan asıl nokta karşımızda baştan keşfedilmeyi bekleyen bir hikaye yok. “Harry Potter” zaten biliniyor. Karakterleri, hikayenin önemli dönü noktalarını, Hogwarts’ı ve hatta filmlerdeki bazı sahneleri bilmeyen bir izleyici bulmak bugün eskisine göre daha zordur. Buna rağmen hikaye yeniden anlatılıyor. Üstelik eski filmlerinin şu an bile tekrar tekrar izlendiği bir dönemde.

Bu nedenle çıkacak diziyi yalnızca “eski filmlerin yenisi” olarak değerlendirmek doğru olmayabilir. Asıl soru, neden zaten bildiğimiz bir hikayeye tekrar ihtiyaç duyulduğu. “Harry Potter”ın yeniden çekilmesi, son yıllarda giderek daha fazla karşılaştığımız bir eğilimin parçası. Hollywood bir süredir eski filmlere geri dönüyor. Yeniden çekimler, devam filmleri, yan hikayeler ve yeniden başlatılan seriler artık çok daha fazla çıkıyor. İnsanlarda alıştıkları filmleri, karakterleri izlemeyi yeni bir şey tanımaktan daha rahat buluyor. Remake yapımlar da bekledikleri ilgiyi çoğunlukla alıyorlar.

Bu nostaljinin nasıl bir tüketim alanına dönüştüğünden bahsedebiliriz. Çünkü nostalji yalnızca iyi kötü geçmişe dönmekle ilgili değil artık geçmişte sevdiğimiz şeylere bugün yeniden ulaşabilmenin, onları satın alabilmenin, izleyebilmenin ve farklı biçimlerde hayatımıza dahil edebilmenin de bir yolu. “Harry Potter” buna iyi bir örnek. Çocukluğunda izlediğin bir filmi yıllar sonra tekrar izlemek başka bir şeyken, o dünyanın bir parçasını bugün satın alabilmek, koleksiyonunu yapmak geçmişi sadece hatırlamakla kalmayıp doğrudan satın alınabilir bir deneyime dönüştürüyor.

Gelecek olan dizi de şimdilik bu döngünün devamı gibi duruyor. Hikaye yeniden anlatılırken yalnızca eski izleyici değil, yeni izleyici de bu evrene dahil ediliyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Enflasyon ve OVP kıskacında emekçiler: Sermayeye teşvik, faize bütçe, çalışana yoksulluk
content:
Andaç Aydın Arıduru [email protected]

Türkiye ekonomisinde 2022 yılı sonrasını kapsayan orta vadeli programlar (OVP) dönemi, ekonomik büyümenin sürdüğü ancak çalışanların milli gelirden aldığı payın gerilediği bir süreç oldu. Bu yıllarda gerçekleşen enflasyona karşılık, şirketlerin ödediği kurumlar vergisindeki artış yüzde 55 seviyesinde kalırken; ücretlilerden kesilen gelir vergisindeki artış yüzde 311’e ulaştı. Bütçe kaynaklarının ağırlıklı olarak faiz ve sermaye teşviklerine aktarıldığı bu dönemde, ücret-maaş zamları geçmiş enflasyon yerine hedeflenen enflasyona göre sınırlandırıldı ve asgari ücret kalıcı olarak açlık sınırının altında bırakıldı.

2023 yılı sonundan 2025 yılı sonuna kadar gerçekleşen yüzde 89’luk enflasyon karşısında merkezi yönetim bütçe verileri, kamu kaynaklarının dağılımındaki değişimi ortaya koydu. Ücretlilerden kesilen gelir vergisi tevkifatı 639 milyar 539 milyon TL’den, yüzde 311 artışla 2 trilyon 630 milyar 180 milyon TL’ye çıktı. Buna karşılık, şirketlerden alınan kurumlar vergisi 786 milyar 318 milyon TL’den, sadece yüzde 55 artarak 1 trilyon 223 milyar 874 milyon TL’ye yükseldi. Şirketlerin vergi artışı, enflasyonun gerisinde kalarak reel olarak azaldı.

Faiz giderleri 674 milyar 614 milyon TL’den yüzde 204 büyüyerek 2 trilyon 54 milyar 382 milyon TL’ye ulaştı. Sanayi ve Teknoloji Bakanlığının sermayeye teşvik ödemeleri 6 milyar 999 milyon TL’den yüzde 322 artışla 29 milyar 582 milyon TL’ye çıktı. Öte yandan, sağlık, emeklilik ve sosyal yardım giderleri 814 milyar 480 milyon TL’den 1 trilyon 931 milyar 724 milyon TL’ye çıkarken artış yüzde 137’de kaldı. Tarımsal destekleme ödemeleri ise 63 milyar 325 milyon 662 bin 660 TL’den 158 milyar 548 milyon TL’ye, sosyal amaçlı transferler ise 78 milyar 93 milyon TL’den 175 milyar 173 milyon 400 bin TL’ye ulaştı. Sosyal güvenlik ve tarım destekleri, faiz ile teşvik kalemlerindeki büyümenin çok gerisinde gerçekleşti.

OVP metinlerinde “Tarımsal ürünlerin alım fiyatları... Geçmiş enflasyona endeksleme davranışının azaltılmasına yardımcı olacak şekilde belirlenecektir” hedefi yer aldı. Maaş zamları sapan enflasyon hedeflerine bağlandı. OVP (2022-2024) belgesinde 2022 yılı için hedeflenen yüzde 9.8’lik enflasyon, yüzde 64.27 olarak gerçekleşti. 2023 yılı için yüzde 8.0 hedeflenirken gerçekleşme yüzde 64.77 oldu. 2024 yılı için yüzde 7.6 olan ilk hedef önce yüzde 33.0’a ve ardından yüzde 41.5’e revize edildi, yıl sonu ise yüzde 44.38 ile kapandı. 2025 yılı için belirlenen yüzde 17.5’lik hedef yüzde 30.89 beklentisiyle aşıldı. 2026 yılı için öngörülen yüzde 9.7’lik enflasyon tahmini ise temmuz 2026 itibarıyla yüzde 31.75 seviyesine geldi.

OVP’lerde, “Ücret-fiyat sarmalının önlenmesine yönelik asgari ücret artışlarının dezenflasyon süreciyle uyumu gözetilmeye devam edilecektir” ifadesiyle ücretler sınırlandı. DİSK-AR Tarafından hazırlanan asgari ücret 2026 raporuna göre, 1974 yılında asgari ücretin kişi başına gayrisafi yurt içi hasılaya (GSYH) oranı yüzde 80.6 iken, bu oran 2025 yılında yüzde 43.6’ya indi. Özel sektör çalışanlarının yüzde 46.7’si asgari ücret ve altında, yüzde 62.5’i ise asgari ücretin yüzde 20 fazlası ve altındaki bantta yer aldı. Toplu iş sözleşmesi kapsama oranı yüzde 10.2’de kalarak asgari ücreti bir ortalama ücrete dönüştürdü.

Kasım 2025 itibarıyla 22 bin 104 TL olan net asgari ücret, 26 bin 925 TL olan açlık sınırının yüzde 18 gerisine düştü. 2000 yılında brüt asgari ücretin 21.9 katı olan ilk gelir vergisi dilimi, 2025’te 6.1 katına düşürüldü ve ücretliler daha erken üst vergi dilimlerine girdi. Bu durum hazinenin gelir vergisi gelirlerinin patlamasına sebep oldu.

2021 yılında yüzde 11.0 oranında büyüme kaydedildi. İş gücünün payı yüzde 30.2’de kaldı. OVP’nin yüzde 16.2’lik enflasyon hedefi yüzde 36.08 gerçekleşme ile katlandı.

2022 yılında emeğin milli gelirden aldığı pay yüzde 26.5’e inerek dip yaptı, sermaye payı yüzde 54.5 ile zirveye çıktı. Yüzde 9.8 enflasyon hedeflenirken yüzde 64.27 oranında enflasyon gerçekleşti. 2023 yılında asgari ücret yılda iki kez artırıldı. İş gücünün payı yüzde 32.8’e yükseldi. 2024 yılında asgari ücrete ara zam yapılmadı. GSYH yüzde 3.2 büyüdü, yıl sonu enflasyonu yüzde 44.38 oldu.

2025 yılında asgari ücret zammı yüzde 30 olarak uygulandı. GSYH yüzde 3.6 büyürken iş gücünün payı yüzde 36.9’a geriledi, sermaye payı yüzde 44.1’e çıktı. author: Unknown
title: İsrail’de seçimler yaklaşırken: Netanyahu’nun rakibi Gadi Eisenkot öne çıkıyor
content:
Fotoğraf: יהב טרודלר (Yahav Studio‬‏), CC BY-SA 3.0

İsrail 27 Ekim 2026 Salı günü yapılacak seçimlere yaklaşırken, Eski İsrail Genelkurmay Başkanı Gadi Eisenkot, Benyamin Netanyahu’nun en önemli rakiplerinden biri haline geldi. Yeni kurduğu “Yaşar” Partisinin kamuoyundaki desteğinin arttığı yeni anketlerde görülüyor.

İsrail’in merkez çizgideki Kanal 12 televizyonu dahil olmak üzere birçok anket, Yaşar Partisinin Netanyahu liderliğindeki Likud Partisinin yanı sıra eski sağcı Başbakan Naftali Bennett ile Yair Lapid tarafından yönetilen muhalefetteki Yahad partisinden de önde olduğunu gösterdi. Bu sonuçlar, Eisenkot’un farklı siyasi kesimler arasındaki nüfuzunun arttığını ortaya koyuyor.

Netanyahu’yu eleştiren Haaretz gazetesi Eisenkot’un mütevazı ve pragmatik olduğunu yazarken Netanyahu’yu destekleyen sağcı Kanal 14, Eisenkot’un “solcu politikaları” olarak nitelendirdiği başlıkları bir uyarı mahiyetinde sıraladı. Kanal, Eisenkot’un hükümet karşıtı protestocuları desteklediğini ve Filistinli partilerle koalisyona girebileceğini söylüyor.

Yaşar Partisinin programının en önemli öncelikleri arasında, İsrail toplumundaki “Çatlakları onarmak” ve Netanyahu hükümetinin saldırılarının hedefi olan medya ve yargı dahil demokratik kurumları güçlendirmek yer alıyor. “Herkes için kamu hizmeti” yasasının onaylanması da bu partinin öncelikleri arasındadır.

Bu yasanın amacı, zorunlu askerlikten muaf tutulan aşır dindar Yahudiler ve İsrailli Arap vatandaşlar dahil tüm vatandaşlar için askerlik veya ulusal hizmeti zorunlu kılmaktır. Bazı muhalefet liderlerinin Filistinli partilerle koalisyon kurma konusunda uyarıda bulunmasının aksine Eisenkot, koalisyon hükümeti kurmasına yardımcı olması için Mansur Abbas liderliğindeki Birleşik Arap listesine dayanma ihtimalini dışlamadı.

Eisenkot, Netanyahu ile karşı karşıya olabilir ancak bir o kadar askeri yapılanmalar için sert ve insanlık dışı hamleleri destekliyor.

Gadi Eisenkot, 19 Mayıs 1960’ta İsrail’in kuzeyindeki Tiberias şehrinde doğdu. Annesi ve babası Fas’tan İsrail’e göç eden Yahudilerdi. Kazanması durumunda, doğu Yahudisi kökenlerine sahip ilk İsrail başbakanı olacak.

Gadi Eisenkot, 2015 yılında ordu genel kurmay başkanlığına atanana kadar askeri rütbelerde kademeli olarak yükseldi. 7 Ekim 2023 saldırılarından sonra Eisenkot, Benyamin Netanyahu başkanlığındaki İsrail savaş kabinesine katıldı.

Eisenkot kariyeri boyunca daha sert askeri pozisyonlar benimsemiştir. 2006 Lübnan Savaşı sırasında ortaya çıkan askeri bir strateji olan “Dahiye doktrini”ni tasralayanlardan biri olarak biliniyor. Bu doktrin adını, Hizbullah’ın ana nüfuz merkezi olan Beyrut’un güneyindeki Dahiye’den almıştır. Bu stratejiye göre, çatışma çıkması durumunda, sivil altyapılar da dahil olmak üzere karşı tarafın altyapısına karşı geniş ve orantısız bir güç kullanılır.

Gadi Eisenkot, 30 Haziran’da seçim kampanyasına başlarken “İsrail kazanmalıdır” sloganıyla “tüm İsraillilerin” lideri olma sözü verdi. 7 Ekim 2023 saldırılarına atıfta bulunarak, “7 Ekim felaketinin hükümeti yolun sonuna gelecektir” dedi.

Gadi Eisenkot ayrıca İsrail Kanal 12 televizyonuna verdiği bir röportajda, hiçbir zaman “iki halk için iki devlet” formülünü desteklemediğini söyledi. İsrail-Filistin çatışmasını çözmek için iki devletli çözümü savunanların, bu çatışmanın dini, ulusal ve sosyal boyutlarının karmaşıklığını doğru bir şekilde anlamadığını savunuyor.

Eisenkot, Netanyahu hükümetinin bakanlarının ve milletvekillerinin ocak 2024’te düzenlenen ve Gazze Şeridi’nde İsrail yerleşimleri kurulmasını talep ettikleri konferansa katılımını eleştirdi.

Eisenkot, geniş ulusal mutabakata dayalı politikalar izlenmesini talep etti ve mevcut hükümeti böyle bir yaklaşımı izlemediği için eleştirdi. Şöyle konuştu: “İsrailli askerler adaletsiz bir savaşta, iki ortak amaç olan rehineleri geri getirmek ve Hamas’ı yenmek için omuz omuza savaşırken, başkaları İsrail toplumundaki çatlakları derinleştiren bir programda yer alma fırsatı buluyor.”

Benyamin Netanyahu, Eisenkot’u seçim kampanyasının ana hedeflerinden biri haline getirdi ve onu solcu bir siyasetçi olarak tanıttı; oysa Eisenkot genellikle İsrail siyasetinin merkez çizgisinde yer alıyor ve bazı konularda da sert askeri pozisyonlara sahip bulunuyor. Yani sağcı ve siyonist bir siyasetçi. Bu sadece İsrail içinde değil dünya açısından da bilinmesi gereken bir gerçek. Zira “sol” adına böyle bir figürün öne çıkarılması birçok sağ merkeziyetçi kesimin de işine yarayacaktır.

Benyamin Netanyahu …

title: Kurdish politician Mehdi Zana has died - UPDATE
content:
Mehdi Zana, the former mayor of Amed, has died. Zana had recently been hospitalized and admitted to intensive care due to COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease).


Amed Metropolitan Municipality has announced the funeral program for politician Mehdi Zana, who died on Saturday. In a post shared on the municipality’s social media account, it was announced that a commemoration ceremony for Mehdi Zana, who served as mayor of Amed between 1977 and 1980, will be held tomorrow, Sunday at 11:00 a.m. in front of the Metropolitan Municipality’s main service building.


The announcement said that Zana’s funeral will be held at 1:00 p.m. at the Ulu Mosque, after which he will be buried at Yeniköy Cemetery. Following the burial, condolences will be received at the Liceliler Mourning House.


The message said: “We invite all our people to attend the commemoration ceremony and bid farewell to Mehdi Zana on his final journey.”

title: Protecting your websites against bad bots and attackers with Proof of Work using Anubis
content:
by Martin Weidenauer


At: MiniDebConf Hamburg 2026


https://hamburg2026.mini.debconf.org/talks/16-protecting-your-websites-against-bad-bots-and-attackers-with-proof-of-work-using-anubis/


This talk is about Anubis:

https://github.com/TecharoHQ/anubis


An implementation of Proof of Work which is used for securing websites against bad bots and attackers. In a world full of AI bots, cyber warfare and so on, this is more important than ever.


This talk is for anyone who hosts their own website or web service. Everyone very likely had to deal with attackers and blocking their IPs, user-agents and so on (probably with tools like Fail2ban).


Anubis is a rather straight forward solution without time-intensive configuration and without blocking users completely. So get your precious time back and make your website bot-proof for the 21st century!


The audience get information about a state-of-the-art tool for protecting websites.


I will cover the following:


general description about the increasing bot/attack problem


explanation of what Proof of Work is


an introduction into Anubis and how it works


a bit of configuration details of Anubis


live demonstration


Q&A

title: A Modern Editor Experience for Debian Packaging
content:
by Jelmer Vernooĳ


At: MiniDebConf Hamburg 2026


https://hamburg2026.mini.debconf.org/talks/14-a-modern-editor-experience-for-debian-packaging/


Language servers have transformed how developers write code. Autocompletion, inline diagnostics, hover documentation, and formatting are now commonplace for most programming languages.


This talk introduces debian-lsp, a nascent language server that brings modern editor features to debian/control, debian/changelog, debian/copyright, debian/watch, and friends: syntax diagnostics, autocompletion of package names and control fields, hover documentation pulled straight from policy, and formatting and linting - all inside your editor of choice, whether that's Vim, Emacs, VS Code, or anything else that speaks LSP.


This will feature a quick live demo of the editor experience, then look under the hood at how it's built: the architecture of the language server, how it integrates with existing Debian tooling and data sources, and how codemods can be surfaced as code actions to let your editor apply automated fixes in a single keystroke.

author: mini-DebConf Germany
title: systemd - a summary
content:
by Christoph Zimmermann


At: MiniDebConf Hamburg 2026


https://hamburg2026.mini.debconf.org/talks/8-systemd-a-summary/


systemd – a summary


Few components of the Linux ecosystem have been more controversial since their introduction than systemd, from technical criticism such as the use of binary formats for logging aspects to complete elimination, such as Devuan, a Debian spin that explicitly dispenses with systemd.


Originally intended as a replacement for the aging SystemV-Init, modern systemd includes a range of functions that extend from a flexible init system to name resolution, hypervisor/container functions and support for user accounts across machine boundaries.


In addition to providing historical context, the presentation aims to give an overview of the key components of the current implementation and the project roadmap. Aspects such as the software quality of the implementation and an analysis of its security, a discussion of GitHub metrics, and a presentation of alternatives are parts of the presentation. In addition to the pure presentation of content, the focus is on the exchange of experiences among the audience beyond the questions following the presentation.


The agenda:


History of the project,


Essential components/architecture,


Software quality of the implementation,


Analysis of the security of the code base,


Code/Github metrics,


Alternatives not only in the init area (openrc, dinit, etc.),


Audience discussion,


Outlook.


Prerequisites:


Basic Linux admin skills, systemd basics
