title: Dortmund ready for the 34th International Kurdish Culture Festival
content:
Preparations for the 34th Kurdish Culture Festival in Dortmund are continuing. Federations affiliated with KON-MED have stepped up their efforts in cities across Germany, while their co-chairs have called for strong participation.


Emphasizing that the festival has been an important gathering for 34 years, the co-chairs described participation as a way of strengthening national unity, honoring the martyrs, and reinforcing solidarity.


KAWA Federation ready


The KAWA Federation has intensified its preparations. Officials said they have been making home visits and organizing public meetings, with the aim of both explaining the process to the people and highlighting the importance of the festival. Buses are being organized from various cities, while departure points and times continue to be shared with participants.


KAWA Federation Co-Chair Kerime Barcin drew attention to developments related to the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the importance of honoring the martyrs of the Kurdistan Freedom Struggle, saying: “It is extremely important that the Kurdish people’s struggle has moved from the armed to the political sphere and evolved toward peace. In this context, we regard the strong participation of our people living in Europe as a demonstration of support for the peace perspective put forward by Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan]. Participation represents an expression of this will.”


Barcin said they attach particular importance to the participation of young people and that the cultural program would be rich, adding: “We want our young people to participate strongly in this festival, where Kurdish culture, language and art will take center stage.


We invite all our people, especially women, to embrace their own culture and attend the festival in traditional national clothing.”


Acar: We have completed our preparations


FED-GEL Co-Chair Lokman Acar said that transportation and organizational preparations within the federation had been completed. Acar said, “This festival, which has been held continuously for 34 years, is an expression of the will of our people living in the diaspora to live freely with their own language, culture and identity.”


Pointing out that this year’s festival is taking place amid a different political process, Acar referred to Öcalan’s February 27 Call and said that the mass participation at Newroz celebrations was evidence of support for the process. Drawing attention to the heavy sacrifices made by the Kurdish people in their struggle for freedom, Acar said: “We are in a period when developments that could pave the way for peace are taking place. We are aware of those seeking to sabotage the process through various provocations and other initiatives. Therefore, strong participation in the festival will be an expression of support for the martyrs and the process.”


Acar said they were working with associations, assemblies and institutions operating under the federation to ensure strong participation, adding that buses from Heilbronn and Pforzheim would depart at 5:00 a.m., while buses from other cities would leave from in front of the associations at midnight on Friday.


A contribution to national unity and solidarity


Preparations are largely complete for the 34th International Kurdish Culture Festival, which will be held on September 5 in Dortmund, Germany, under the auspices of the Mesopotamia Federation of Free Societies (FED-MED). FED-MED Co-Chair Ahmet Kobanê said tens of thousands of people from across Europe, particularly France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland and Germany, are expected to gather in Dortmund, and called on everyone to attend the festival.


Speaking about the festival’s cultural and political significance, Kobanê said: “The festival contributes to preserving Kurdish culture and art in the diaspora. Many colors of our culture, from govend to music, from songs to theater, will have a place at the festival. Our festival is also a gathering where we demonstrate our commitment to the martyrs, strengthen national unity, and reinforce solidarity and our common struggle.”


Kobanê said critical developments in the region, particularly in Rojava, Rojhilat and Başûr, have increased the importance of the festival, and noted that the struggle waged in Rojava for many years has entered a new phase. title: Farisoğulları: Democracy is not a favor granted from above
content:
ANF spoke with Musa Farisoğulları, a former Amed MP for the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) and former executive of the Democratic Society Congress (DTK), about the current political atmosphere in Turkey, the “Peace and Democratic Society Process,” the continued practice of appointing trustees despite the process, and the participation of Kurds living in exile in political life.


As you have witnessed, particularly after 2015–2016, Turkey experienced a policy and practice of appointing trustees. How would you assess these trustee appointments in terms of their impact on local democracy or democracy more broadly? This practice is still continuing and, in Kurdish municipalities, is expanding across Turkey to include different political parties as well.


When we assess the 2015 process and July 15 in terms of their consequences, we need to view them as a move by factions within the state. The extraordinary conditions created at the time were used to build a one-man-centered system. During the state of emergency, the focus turned toward the Kurds and democratic forces. Institutions were shut down and thousands of people were dismissed from their positions.


In 2016, the trustee system was institutionalized. Removing elected co-mayors is not merely a transfer of a building; it is the usurpation of the will of tens or hundreds of thousands of citizens. The fact that Kurds were choosing their local administrators through their own will disturbed the central government. However, our warnings at the time — “What is being applied to us today will be applied to you tomorrow” — were not heeded. Today, the trustee regime has become a generalized form of governance extending to opposition parties, CHP municipalities and even companies.


There is currently also a process underway in Turkey. One of the key concepts emerging in this search, which the Kurdish side describes as the “Peace and Democratic Society Process,” is “democratic integration.” On one side is a trustee-based and centralized approach, while on the other is an approach advocating the strengthening of local government. Why do you think local governments are given such importance, and what role can the local level play in developing a democratic society?


This issue is the result of a historical and comprehensive search. Since the 1990s, repeated steps have been taken to end the armed struggle and resolve the issue through democratic politics. On October 1, 2025, MHP leader Bahçeli’s greeting to the DEM Party parliamentary group, followed by his statements, was seen as a sign of moving beyond the old paradigm of “denial and non-recognition.” Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan responded with his February 27 declaration, and negotiations were conducted with a state delegation within this framework.


First, as is known, the PKK dissolved itself at its 12th Congress. Then, in July 2025, a group of 30 guerrillas led by Besê Hozat burned their weapons. Subsequently, as is known, the guerrillas withdrew from certain areas.


These steps should not be approached as ordinary developments. First, a commission was established in parliament, followed by a legal amendment. However, despite all these steps and symbolic moves taken by the Kurdish side, Turkey has not yet taken concrete steps toward corresponding legal and legislative arrangements. In other words, the steps taken by the Turkish side are not commensurate with those taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement; they are insufficient and do not meet them.


On the other hand, the concept of “democratic integration” you mentioned comes into play precisely here. Democratic integration is not a unilateral imposition or surrender; it means the two sides meeting on an equal and voluntary basis under new conditions. The Kurds did not wage war against the peoples of Turkey; the problem was with the state system. For the laying down of arms and the process to move forward, this situation must be placed on a legal and constitutional footing. Although it has shortcomings, the Framework Law passed through parliament. However, there is a need for a legal and political foundation that will give society confidence.


You have been abroad for a long time and have had the opportunity to observe developments. A significant proportion of Kurds live in exile. Why do you think it is important for Kurds living in exile to participate in political life in the countries where they reside? How do you observe their participation? …

title: Assets of 12 Iraqi MPs and officials seized
content:
The Central Bank of Iraq has published documents concerning a decision to seize the assets of certain government officials and members of parliament.


According to the documents, the Karkh Investigation Court, which handles corruption cases, ordered the seizure of the assets of 12 MPs and former advisers to the Iraqi prime minister.


The Central Bank of Iraq also reportedly instructed all private and public banks to freeze all bank accounts belonging to these individuals, who are as follows:

title: PUK official welcomes Öcalan’s proposal for a “Democratic Unity Government” in the Kurdistan Region
content:

Peace is one of the PUK’s fundamental principles, because the people of Kurdistan can achieve their rights only through peace and democracy.”


Referring to Abdullah Öcalan’s proposal for the establishment of a “Democratic Unity Government” in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, Ziyad Jabar said: “Mr. Öcalan’s message calling for the unity of our people and for us to have a united government is a friendly and sincere message.”

title: MP Sarıtaş: Öcalan’s freedom should be the first of the next steps
content:
With the ‘Framework Law’ passed by the Turkish Parliament as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, issues excluded from the scope of the legislation have once again come to the fore. Although the law contains provisions concerning disarmament and the related legal processes, the absence of any provisions regarding Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom and legal status has become one of the key issues of debate concerning the next stage of the process. It is believed that steps toward securing Öcalan’s physical freedom and defining his legal status will be decisive for the future of the Peace and Democratic Society Process and for achieving a democratic and lasting solution to the Kurdish question.


DEM Party Siirt MP Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş spoke to ANF about the ongoing process in search of peace and democratization in Turkey.


‘The law is

the most concrete and practical step’


Emphasizing the significance of the law, Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş said:


“First of all, the law was passed after a very long delay and with many shortcomings, but perhaps with a voting majority and level of representation rarely seen in the history of the Turkish Parliament. This law is important to us. We can say that it is the most concrete and practical step taken in a process that has been underway for a year and a half—or rather, nearly two years.


In our work on the ground, we have encountered concerns such as, ‘Why isn’t the state taking any steps?’ and ‘We don’t trust the process.’ To some extent, and of course depending on how the law is to be implemented in practice, the fact that a step has now been taken will help build confidence within society. The question ‘Could it really happen?’ has now begun to gain some ground in public opinion. At least, that is the case within our community.”


What matter is how the law will be put into practice’


Pointing to the importance of discussions surrounding the implementation of the law, Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş said:


“The implementation of the law is extremely important. Because how it will be implemented from this point onward matters; having it merely in writing is not enough—the real question is how it will be put into practice. Yes, it exists in written form, but how will it work in practice? For example, how will the returns take place? How will releases from prisons be carried out?


Therefore, the practical implementation of the steps to be taken in the coming period is crucial both for the fate and the successful continuation of the process. The ongoing talks and the commissions being established are important. As you know, a board will be formed, along with its sub-commissions. There will be three components referred to publicly as TDYK: Determination, Verification and Commitment. Everyone is eagerly awaiting to see how the commission responsible for the commitment phase—which Kurdish People’s Leader Mr. Abdullah Öcalan will actively participate in and coordinate—will operate in practice.”


‘Delays

have caused concern’


Stating that delays in the Democratic Society Process have caused concern within society, Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş said: “What we have been saying throughout this process is that the delays in a process that has been ongoing for two years—which have caused concern and anxiety among the public—must not continue in the next phase. Therefore, these commissions need to be established as soon as possible and begin operating in practice.”


‘

Thousands of political prisoners are awaiting release’


Emphasizing that the process is not limited solely to legal arrangements, Sabahat Erdoğan Sarıtaş drew attention to the situation of political prisoners and the return of Kurdish politicians living in Europe or elsewhere in the diaspora:


“There are thousands of political prisoners awaiting release. Another matter is the return of many Kurdish politicians who have been forced into exile in Europe and across the diaspora because of their political activities and involvement in democratic politics.


And perhaps most importantly, almost everyone is watching closely to see how the returns from rural areas will take place and how members of the freedom movement will return to public life or to the country. Therefore, this is both an extremely important and historic process, which also carries a number of risks and potential pitfalls that could lead to provocations. For that reason, taking these steps from this point onward is important both in practical terms and …

author: Julia Conley
title: Trump Administration Reportedly Nearing Deal to Take Over Venezuelan Oil Fields
content:
“Congress must intervene and put an end to Trump’s oil-fueled imperialism,” said an analyst with Public Citizen.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Trump administration officials are claiming that talks between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the Venezuelan government regarding control of the country’s oil fields will ultimately secure “America’s energy future for generations to come” — but analysts on Friday called on lawmakers to halt President Donald Trump’s “colonial” push to take over the reserves.

As Axios reported, officials including Rubio and Deputy White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller have been involved in talks with Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodriguez about taking an ownership stake in more than a dozen oil fields in the Orinoco Belt and Lake Maracaibo regions, which have about 90 billion barrels of oil reserves. In all, Venezuela’s vast reserves — the world’s largest — contain about 300 billion barrels.

The deal would double US oil reserves at a time when Americans have seen gas prices skyrocket and oil firms reap profits as a result of Trump’s war on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz — events to which countries that have expanded renewable energy sources have proven far more resilient, according to data from JP Morgan Commodities research.

Despite that resilience, the Trump administration has reportedly approached the talks as a way to lock the US into generations of continued reliance on planet-heating oil extraction. According to Bloomberg, one deal under consideration is a 100-year lease on the oil fields.

Axios reported that in return for giving the US an ownership stake — something Trump began privately discussing before US forces invaded Venezuela and abducted President Nicolás Maduro in January — Venezuela “would benefit from private companies, including American firms, developing the fields and returning more oil revenue” to the South American country.

Tyler Slocum, director of Public Citizen’s energy program, said that if the deal is finalized, “Trump will likely transfer operational control to US oil companies,” which donated heavily to his campaign.

The proposed deal would open “the door to Trump’s typical bilateral transactional corruption” and bestow “lucrative opportunities for the oil companies he chooses to reward,” said Slocum.

“In the nearly eight months since Trump’s illegal January 2026 Venezuelan invasion, the Trump administration has managed a $13 billion slush fund gleaned from its control over Venezuelan oil sales, with zero transparency, and little to no public oversight or accounting,” Slocum continued. “The president has no authority to negotiate a deal where the federal government takes control over foreign oil production facilities, and Congress must intervene and put an end to Trump’s oil-fueled imperialism.”

One opposition leader in Venezuela, where Energy Secretary Chris Wright is expected to travel next week to discuss increasing oil production by US companies, said the deals currently being discussed amount to “a land grab — a massive land grab.”

Francisco Rodríguez, a senior research fellow at the Center for Economic and Policy Research and author of The Collapse of Venezuela, said the country’s National Assembly “should deny authorization for this predatory deal.”

Handing over Venezuela's oil wealth to the US contravenes the Constitution and is not in the interest of the Venezuelan people — much more when it is done at gunpoint. Venezuela's National Assembly should deny authorization for this predatory deal.https://t.co/6VaQxu1BOd

Following Trump’s invasion of Venezuela in January, energy historian and Eurasia Group analyst Gregory Brew told The Guardian, “US dominance over Venezuelan oil reserves allows the US to regard Venezuelan reserves as its own reserves: a source of oil from which the United States can draw and that nobody else has access to.”

“I think that’s how the administration is conceiving of this — excluding China, excluding Russia, but I think also excluding other potential customers for Venezuelan oil,” Brew said. “It sounds colonial, because it is.”

The president’s “effort to establish a South American kleptocracy is an outrage,” said Slocum. “There’s been no improvement in human rights in Venezuela, so Trump’s move is further evidence that his illegal actions in Venezuela are all about controlling oil with no public accounting …

author: Mike Ludwig
title: Free Speech Groups Sound Alarm on “Red Scare” Repression of ICE Watch Activists
content:
Advocates asked a court to unseal more details on Trump’s surveillance of churches, schools, and libraries in Minnesota.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Free speech groups across the country are sounding the alarm over the Trump administration’s surveillance of social movements in Minnesota and the prosecution of the Minnesota 15, a group of activists from Minneapolis-St. Paul who face federal conspiracy charges after organizing protests against brutal immigration sweeps earlier this year.

President Donald Trump and his allies in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Justice Department have targeted the First Amendment-protected expression of protesters, civil society groups, journalists, universities, and the lawyers representing them at a scale that has “not been seen since the Second Red Scare,” according to an amicus brief filed with a federal court in Minnesota on August 25 by Protect Democracy and other groups.

Documents recently released in court filings show that DHS agents spied on churches, schools, and libraries to gather information on labor unions, nonprofits, and community groups large and small. In June, the Minnesota 15 were arrested and charged with conspiracy to stalk, impede, and assault immigration officers under a section of federal law the Trump administration has used to arrest anti-ICE protesters across the country.

Instead of attempting to tie the Minnesota 15 to one specific incident, prosecutors filed conspiracy charges linking the defendants to rapid response groups that coordinated to alert people about ICE raids and send volunteers into the streets in response — a loose set of tactics that became a model for anti-ICE organizers elsewhere.

Will Creeley, legal director of the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE), a nonpartisan group that defends speech across the political spectrum, compared Trump’s crackdown on Minnesota to the worst civil liberties abuses during the McCarthy era and COINTELPRO in the mid-20th century. At the time, paranoia about communism ran high on the right, and civil rights organizers, gay federal employees, and anti-war activists were targeted for surveillance, arrest, and interrogation due to perceived disloyalty to the United States or for holding pro-peace, anti-racist, and left-wing political beliefs.

“The idea is to stoke a culture of fear and have folks keep quiet rather than disagree with those in power,” Creeley told Truthout. “But the First Amendment is designed to protect just that kind of disagreement.”

However, by prosecuting the Minnesota 15 for political activism, the Trump administration has been forced through the legal discovery process to reveal details about the federal surveillance of protests against Operation Metro Surge, the immigration crackdown in Minnesota announced by Trump in December.

Documents released by a defense attorney earlier this month show that undercover agents with ICE’s investigative unit infiltrated multiple left-leaning groups in Minneapolis as part of an investigation called “Operation Puppet Master,” four days after a group of federal agents shot and killed Alex Pretti, the nurse who died while attempting to shield another protester from the agents on January 24.

In addition to killing Pretti and protester Renee Good, federal immigration agents terrorized tight-knit neighborhoods in the Twin Cities and across Minnesota in what Human Rights Watch calls a “manufactured crisis.” Protests and mutual aid efforts erupted as videos of violent arrests and confrontations between federal agents and residents went viral, resulting in dozens of arrests.

FIRE, the left-leaning Protect Democracy, the right-leaning Society for the Rule of Law, and the libertarian Cato Institute filed a brief on August 25 in support of a request by a defense attorney representing the Minnesota 15 defendants for the government to hand over more documents and records related to its surveillance of activist groups, including any correspondence between the White House and prosecutors. The coalition reflects growing bipartisan frustration over Trump’s excesses and power grabs.

The groups want additional documents from prosecutors made public to further understand the scope of government surveillance under the controversial NSPM-7 directive, a memo issued by Trump in 2025 that conflates “anti-Americanism” …

author: Randi Beers
title: News quiz Aug. 29 | This one’s for the foodies
content:
It’s back to school time. Good thing we’ve got this quiz to help tone those brain muscles. Let’s get rolling!


1.

 Why were RCMP officers in Rankin Inlet recently photographed eating pickles?


A.

 RCMP are promoting pickleball as a way to connect with community members through sport.


B.

 In an effort to get to know community members better, officers hosted an event where participants debated what they thought was the best garnish.


C.

 There is a pickle thief on the loose, and RCMP posted a photo of themselves eating pickles to attract attention to the issue.


2.

 People in Iqaluit flocked to collect their share of maktaaq after hunters harvested a bowhead whale last week. How much does a bowhead hunt cost for equipment, payment to crew, food and fuel?


A.

 $100,000


B.

 $120,000


C.

 $140,000


3.

 The U.S.-Canada trade war is in the headlines again after Canadian delegates walked away from negotiations on Aug. 21. After U.S. tariffs against Canada went into effect over the weekend, Canada announced a list of items it will target with retaliatory tariffs, starting Sept. 8. Which food product is included in the list?


A.

 Beef


B.

 Seafood


C.

 Oranges


4.

 Trichinella, a parasitic infection that can be deadly, was detected in what animal recently harvested near Naujaat?


A.

 Polar bear


B.

Seal


C.

 Walrus


5.

 Speaking of walrus, who is taking viewers on a walrus hunt for the first episode of

Go North!

, a new docuseries that examines Indigenous resilience and the land?


A.

 Terry Uyarak


B.

 Zacharias Kunuk


C.

 Jordin Tootoo


Answers:


Maqtaaq, bowhead whale meat, awaits pick up on Monday afternoon at the Iqaluit breakwater. (Photo by Daron Letts)


1. A — Sgt. Darick Ramminger bought a net, five paddles and balls, and he’s

ready to challenge

 people to a game of pickleball in Rankin Inlet. He hopes police can eventually organize a tournament.


2. B — The price to

host

 this year’s bowhead hunt in Iqaluit was $120,000. The cost was covered by Nunavut Tunngavik Inc., Qikiqtani Inuit Association, Baffin Fisheries Coalition and the City of Iqaluit.


3. B — Seafood is

on the list

 of Canada’s retaliatory tariffs set to go into effect Sept. 8. On the list are also appliances, paper products, tableware and furniture.


4. C — Trichinella was

detected in a walrus

 recently harvested in Naujaat. People in the community who develop symptoms like stomach pain, muscle pain, diarrhea, swollen eyelids, sweating or weakness, and who have recently eaten walrus, should report to the health centre, the Health Department says.


5. A — Musician Terry Uyarak is

taking a television crew

 with him on a walrus hunt outside Igloolik for the first episode of

Go North!

, which is set to première Sept. 3 on APTN.

author: Helmut Weiss
title: Taser sind harmlos? Sagt das den Toten…
content:
Dossier


„

In Frankfurt ist ein 49 Jahre alter Mann wenige Tage nach einem Polizeieinsatz gestorben, bei dem er in seiner Wohnung im Ostend mit einem Taser außer Gefecht gesetzt worden war. Wie Nadja Niesen, die Sprecherin der Frankfurter Staatsanwaltschaft, der Frankfurter Rundschau bestätigte, werde in dem Fall gegen zwei Polizisten wegen des Verdachts auf Körperverletzung mit Todesfolge im Amt ermittelt…

“ – aus dem

Bericht „Mann stirbt nach Taser-Einsatz der Polizei“ von Pitt v. Bebenburg und Hanning Voigts am 11. Mai 2019 in der FR online


, der nur einer von vielen und zunehmenden ist… Siehe in unserem Dossier zu Tasern in Deutschland auch Beiträge über weitere (Todes)Opfer sowie über (ziemlich alte) Proteste gegen die Einführung und zynische Reaktionen von Behörden und Verantwortlichen in den Landesregierungen:


Nach dem Tod von Ibrahima Barry in Polizeigewahrsam beginnt der Prozess gegen 9 Polizisten – lediglich wegen schwerer Körperverletzung im Amt


Prozess gegen neun Polizisten in Düsseldorf wegen des Todes von Ibrahima Barry: Gutachten zum Tod von geflüchtetem Guineer belastet Polizisten


„

Im Prozess gegen neun Polizisten in Düsseldorf wegen des Todes von Ibrahima Barry liefert Forensic Architecture neue Beweise für Vorwürfe der Nebenklage.


Am Donnerstag wurde vor dem Landgericht Duisburg der Prozess um den Tod des Geflüchteten Ibrahima Barry fortgesetzt. Angeklagt sind vier Polizistinnen und fünf Polizisten wegen gemeinschaftlich begangener gefährlicher Körperverletzung im Amt. Sie hatten den damals 23-jährigen Guineer im sogenannten Flüchtlingsdorf Saarn in Mülheim an der Ruhr fortwährend herablassend angeschrien, zweimal getasert und bis zu seinem Tod gewaltsam fixiert. Dass erst diese Fesselung zum Tod Barrys geführt hat, soll nun ein Gutachten belegen, das die Nebenklage-Anwältinnen Anna Busl und Andrea Groß-Bölting am Donnerstagabend in einer Pressekonferenz vorgestellt haben. Die Polizist*innen hatten den wimmernden jungen Mann über einen längeren Zeitraum in der sogenannten »Hogtie«-Position fixiert und seine Hände und Füße dazu in Bauchlage gefesselt und auf dem Rücken miteinander verbunden. (…)


Eine angebliche Notwehrlage bestand spätestens ab dem Zeitpunkt nicht mehr, als einer der Angeklagten per Funk an die Zentrale meldete, die Lage sei unter Kontrolle. Von da an hätte Barry laut Lehrmeinung in eine sitzende oder seitliche Position gebracht werden müssen. Stattdessen standen die Beamt*innen mehr als zehn Minuten um ihn herum, wie die Bodycam-Aufnahmen belegen – ohne auf seine Hyperventilation, seine leiser werdende Stimme oder seinen Stuhlabgang zu reagieren. »Der hat sich eingeschissen«, sind Beamte feixend zu hören. Zwei von ihnen ziehen daraufhin Barrys Hose hoch. Dass eine solche Defäkation auf eine drohende Erstickung verweist, hätten mindestens die Sanitäter*innen wissen müssen.


Tod Barrys billigend in Kauf genommen?


Die Nebenklage argumentiert, dass die aggressive Fesselung und die über zehn Minuten aufrechterhaltene Bauchlage todesursächlich gewesen seien. »Damit stellt sich aber auch die Frage, ob die Angeklagten den Tod Barrys zumindest billigend in Kauf genommen haben. Schließlich ist der lagebedingte Erstickungstod Teil der Ausbildung und die Gefahren einer Fesselung in Bauchlage daher bekannt«, sagt die Nebenklageanwältin Busl zu »nd«

…“

Artikel von Matthias Monroy vom 28.08.2026 in ND online

 


Nach Tod von Ibrahima Barry: Beamte schweigen vor Gericht. Die Anklage wirft ihnen eine rechtswidrige und gefährliche Fesselung vor, sieht aber keine Schuld am Tod – ein juristischer Widerspruch mit Sprengkraft


„Nach dem Tod des Geflüchteten Ibrahima Barry bei einem Polizeieinsatz in Mülheim an der Ruhr müssen sich seit Mittwoch neun Polizeibeamten vor dem Landgericht Duisburg verantworten. Die Anklage lautet auf gemeinschaftliche gefährliche Körperverletzung im Amt. Die fünf Polizisten und vier Polizistinnen sollen Barry am 6. Januar 2024 an Händen und Füßen gefesselt und beide Fesselungen anschließend mit Kabelbindern auf dem Rücken verbunden haben. Nach Darstellung der Anklage war diese zusätzliche Verbindung weder nach dem Polizeigesetz noch nach dem Strafgesetzbuch gerechtfertigt. (…) Als Todesursache nennt die Anklage eine Kombination aus einem lagebedingten Erstickungstod, einem Herzinfarkt, Kokaineinfluss, einem Erregungszustand und einer Lungenkrankheit. Auch unabhängig ist die Einordnung des Falls brisant. Denn obwohl die Staatsanwaltschaft die …

title: (Warn)Streik des Pflegepersonals für Entlastung durch tarifliche Personalbemessung an der Charité
content:
Dossier


Seit zwei Jahren verhandelt ver.di mit dem Vorstand der Charité über Mindestbesetzungsregelung und Maßnahmen zum Gesundheitsschutz für alle Beschäftigten an der Charité. Der Vorstand hatte zuletzt Regelungen für die Intensivstationen und eine Aufstockung der sog. „Nachtdienstverbünde“ angeboten. Dies brächte eine Verbesserung für ca. 700 der über 13.000 Beschäftigten. Der Charité-Vorstand bleibt auch nach zwei Jahren Verhandlungen ein Angebot schuldig, mit dem eine Verbesserung der Arbeitsbedingungen für alle Beschäftigten erreicht werden kann. Auch beim „Konsequenzenmanagement“ (Entlastungsregelungen für den Fall, dass Personalvorgaben nicht eingehalten werden können) macht die Charité kein belastbares Angebot. Nach der massiven Beteiligung am Warnstreik vom 27.-28. April 2015 sorgt das Verhalten der Geschäftsführung für großes Unverständnis unter den Beschäftigten der Charité. Die ver.di-Tarifkommission sieht vor diesem Hintergrund in dem Arbeitgeberangebot keine Basis für weitere Verhandlungen… Siehe zu Hintergründen, Aktionen, Solierklärungen und Aufrufen

die ver.di-Aktionsseite


. Solidaritätserklärungen willkommen! Bitte sendet diese an:

info@mehr-krankenhauspersonal.de.

Siehe dazu neu:


Kampf um Entlastung 2.0: ver.di ruft an der Charité vom 2.-4.9. in den Streik, um den Tarifvertrag Gesundheitsfachberufe zu verteidigen und weiterzuentwickeln


„

Im Jahr 2021 haben die Beschäftigten der Charité mit dem Tarifvertrag Gesundheitsfachberufe einen tariflichen Anspruch auf Entlastung in einem 30-tägigen Erzwingungsstreik erkämpft. Er regelt Personalvorgaben für viele Bereiche in Europas größtem Universitätsklinikum.


Nach fast fünf Jahren Erfahrung mit dem Tarifvertrag treten die Beschäftigten nun an, um den Tarifvertrag weiterzuentwickeln. So klammert der Tarifvertrag aktuell einzelne Beschäftigtengruppen und Bereiche an der Charité aus. Auch haben sich einige Regelungen als nicht ausreichend für eine Entlastung erwiesen. Auch die Regelungen zur Ausbildung müssen nach Einschätzung der ver.di Tarifkommission verbessert werden. Für die zahlreichen aus dem Ausland angeworbenen Pflegefachkräfte fordern die Beschäftigten mehr Unterstützung bei Einarbeitung und Integration.


Vor diesem Hintergrund hat die ver.di Tarifkommission den Vorstand der Charité zu Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Bisher fanden zwei Verhandlungsrunden statt.  Doch statt konstruktiv über eine Nachbesserung und Schärfung der Regelungen zu verhandeln, werden bisher gut funktionierende Regelungen  zur Disposition gestellt. Von den Kolleg:innen werden Verschlechterungen ihrer Arbeitsbedingungen per Tarifvertrag gefordert. Damit blockiert der Charité-Vorstand aktuell Fortschritte in den Verhandlungen.


Deshalb ruft ver.di ab nächster Woche zum Streik auf. Am Montag finden begrenzte Streikaktivitäten statt. Von Mittwoch bis Freitag (2.09.-4.09.), ruft ver.di zu umfassenden Streikmaßnahmen auf, die einer deutlichen Einschränkung im Krankenhausbetrieb führen können. ver.di stellt für den Zeitraum sicher, dass ausreichend Personal für die Behandlung von Notfällen bereit gestellt wird. Es ist mit deutlichen Einschränkungen bei planbaren Behandlungen zu rechnen

…“

Pressemitteilung vom 28.8.2026 beim ver.di-Landesbezirk Berlin-Brandenburg

 


Siehe zu den aktuellen gesetzlichen Hintergründen auch das Dossier

Pflegebudget: Der Kampf um Personalbesetzung und Pflegepersonaluntergrenzen


Vor Verhandlungen am 30. Juli fordert ver.di, den Entlastungstarifvertrag an der Charité fortzusetzen und wo nötig nachzubessern – trotz der Bundesgesetzgebung


Entlastungstarifvertrag an der Charité: gute Arbeitsbedingungen und gute Versorgung sichern statt Politik auf dem Rücken der Beschäftigten


„Die Gewerkschaft ver.di fordert, den Entlastungstarifvertrag an der Charité, der gute Personalausstattungen für Pflege und andere Berufsgruppen sichert, trotz der aktuellen Bundesgesetzgebung fortzusetzen und wo nötig nachzubessern. Eine Verschlechterung des Tarifvertrags und damit der Arbeits- und Versorgungsbedingungen lehnen die ver.di-Mitglieder entschieden ab.


Die Forderungen, die in den letzten Wochen in weit mehr als der Hälfte der Teams diskutiert, in der Vorwoche von über 200 Kolleginnen und Kollegen diskutiert und von der ver.di Tarifkommission beschlossen worden waren, wurden am 15.07. in der ersten Verhandlungsrunde mit der Arbeitgeberin vorgestellt.


Die Kolleginnen und Kollegen an der Charité gehen gut vorbereitet, professionell und mit klaren …

title: Gülistan Doku investigation: 10 people taken into custody
content:
A fifth wave of operations was carried out as part of the investigation into the disappearance of Gülistan Doku in Dêrsim. Ten people were detained as part of the investigation. New findings have been uncovered, including new PTS and communication records, suspicious access to and activity on Gülistan Doku’s Instagram account, and new evidence concerning underwater searches.


It was reported that records in a diver’s logbook, which had been determined to have been concealed from judicial authorities, did not match the official search reports. It was also stated that evidence had been obtained suggesting that some of Gülistan Doku’s personal belongings may have been placed underwater at a later stage in order to create the appearance of evidence supporting the possibility of suicide.

author: Unknown
title: Veysi Aktaş: Our resistance must be as great as the dreams of the martyrs
content:
As a condolence gathering held for the Kurdistan Freedom Martyrs in the Cizîra Botan district of Şirnex came to an end on its third day, a commemoration was held under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture of Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER).


Thousands of people from Cizre Botan and surrounding provinces and districts attended the commemoration, held in front of the DEM Party’s Cizre district office, along with families of the martyrs and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.


Entering the commemoration area to slogans of “Long Live Leader Apo” and “Martyrs are Immortal,” accompanied by ululations, people placed photographs of Leader Apo and the martyrs on the platform. The platform also displayed Leader Apo’s words: “My martyred comrades and I worked along the path of love. Those who remain must know how to walk this path.”


Photographs of Mahsum Korkmaz (Egîd), one of the PKK’s first commanders, and Zeynep Kınacı (Zîlan) were also displayed, alongside a large photograph of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan].


The program began with a moment of silence, followed by the singing of the “Çarxa Şoreşê” anthem.


“We will never forget them”


Speaking at the commemoration, MEBYA-DER executive Esmer Çıkmaz said that, as the families of martyrs, they would continue the struggle for peace and freedom.


Esmer Çıkmaz said, “As mothers, we made them a promise: We will bring peace and freedom to this country. We will never forget them. We will bring peace and freedom to this country.”


“To honor the martyrs is to uphold their goal”


DEM Party Mêrdîn MP Beritan Güneş Altın noted that people from different parts of Kurdistan had attended the commemoration and paid tribute to the martyrs.


Stating that honoring the martyrs means upholding their goals, Beritan Güneş Altın said: “To honor the martyrs means to uphold their goals, to create a democratic society. To honor the martyrs means to uphold Leader Apo’s paradigm and to uphold peace.”


Beritan Güneş Altın said that Öcalan’s physical freedom must be secured, adding, “Those who ask what the Kurdish people want should look at this photograph. The Kurdish people want peace despite their pain; they want to live together.”


Veysi Aktaş, a member of the Imralı Secretariat, said that Cizre Botan is the land of the story of Mem û Zîn, describing the martyrs as the contemporary representatives of that story.


Aktaş said: “Every male comrade who has fallen as a martyr is Mem. Every female comrade who has fallen as a martyr is Zîn. Because, just like Mem, they gave their lives for freedom.”


Saying that the martyrs fought for a free future, Aktaş stated, “Each of our martyrs is a hero who completes the unfinished story of Mem and Zîn with a free future.”


“Our resistance must be as great as their dreams”


Aktaş said that the martyrs were not merely fighters, but people who struggled to build a democratic and equal society, adding: “Every woman and man who fell as a martyr waged this resistance not only for themselves, but to liberate an entire society.


Our resistance must be as great as their dreams; their spirit is a source of strength and inspiration for us.”


“Everyone should take their place in democratic politics”


Referring to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Aktaş said that the people must participate in the process and called for participation in democratic politics. He added: “That is why we are beginning a new struggle. We are beginning democratic politics. Let everyone take their place here. Our destiny depends on us.”

author: Unknown
title: Doğan: Öcalan must have the conditions to fulfil his historic role
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan held a press conference at the party’s headquarters on the Central Executive Board meeting held on Thursday, 27 August, and current developments.


Ayşegül Doğan said: “The framework law, developments in Syria, the resistance of Doruk Mining workers, the condolence gatherings held recently and missing-person notices were discussed extensively. Of course, another important issue was the congress we will hold on 6 September.”


Framework law: Coordinated work


Ayşegül Doğan began her remarks with the framework law and continued: “The Monitoring and Evaluation Board, which will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the process under the law, has been established. The Monitoring and Evaluation Board held its first meeting on 24 August. Our Central Executive Board considers the fact that it held its first meeting and began its work to be a highly significant development. To coordinate the work, a total of four bodies have been established: the Judicial and Legal Affairs Board, the Monitoring and Assessment Board, the Social Cohesion and Integration Subcommittee, and the Disarmament and Strategy Coordination Subcommittee. One of our greatest expectations is that these bodies will work inclusively and in coordination with one another, in keeping with the pace of the historic process we are going through. We believe that, in the coming period, it will become clearer how these bodies will work, who will serve on them, and how they will coordinate and work in concert with one another.”


Mechanisms that include different sections of society


Doğan said: “Even before these boards began to be established, we had been saying the same thing from the very first day of the process: this cannot be confined solely to a bureaucratic mechanism. We are talking about a demand for peace and democracy, and about making that demand a reality. There is an immense and considerable effort in Turkey in this regard. That effort must also feed into these boards, and this contribution must be reflected in their work. What do I mean by this? We need to create opportunities for civil society to contribute and for people with experience in this field to bring the knowledge they have accumulated over the years into these boards, while also enabling them to follow the process. In other words, it would be beneficial to effectively put in place mechanisms that can include different sections of society in these boards. As always, this was one of the critical points we discussed within our Central Executive Board. We call this the Peace and Democratic Society Process. We are talking about a process of building something new, and we have all experienced and seen how critical it is for society’s support to be directly visible in this process.”


Conditions for Abdullah Öcalan


Doğan also said: “Another expectation of ours, and another critical issue, is that Mr. Öcalan must be provided with the opportunities and conditions necessary to carry out the weighty and historic responsibility he has assumed in this process. As you know, this is not something we are saying for the first time. Every stage we have gone through so far has shown us why he needs to take part in this process effectively, with conditions that allow for uninterrupted communication. This is not only a matter of coordinating disarmament. To put it in Mr. Öcalan’s own words, another point that is highly critical for our party is that his position in this process must be clearly defined and that he must be placed in a position where he can provide coordination in order to make the historic Kurdish-Turkish alliance and coexistence permanent. Mr. Öcalan also says, ‘Let us build a shared life together, with the awareness that patiently opening this path is a historic opportunity, and by abandoning simplistic, narrow approaches that do not serve the future.’ We strongly underline these words. In doing so, we also want to offer a reminder about language. The language of this new period must also be shaped by new expressions and new words. Instead of language that constantly accuses, questions and judges, we must be able to develop a language through which we can empathise with one another, while taking mutual sensitivities into consideration. This is another issue to which our party attaches great importance.”


We are at the heart of the transition from conflict to non-conflict

author: Unknown
title: Karayılan: Our martyrs sacrificed themselves for the success of our people
content:
Murat Karayılan, a member of the People’s Defense Center (HSM) Command, answered ANF’s questions and spoke about the recently announced deaths of guerrilla fighters, the commemorations and condolence gatherings held in many cities across Kurdistan, the reasons for the delay in announcing the deaths, the status of the remains, and solidarity with the families of those who lost their lives. 


Part one of this interview can be read

here

. 


What can you say about the families’ requests to recover the remains of the martyr guerrillas? Of course, deaths are a reality of war in a struggle for freedom that has lasted for more than 50 years. Yet the remains of very few guerrillas are handed over to their families. The whereabouts of many of the martyrs are not even known. Families are making strong and persistent demands to recover the remains of their loved ones. What can you say about this?


This is also an important issue for us. As is known, from the Republican era to the present day, because they sought to annihilate our society, Kurdish society, they wanted the heroes to be forgotten and not commemorated; they aimed to erase our memory. In other words, they wanted us to lose our history. For this reason, from the very beginning until today, the locations of the graves of those who lost their lives in the Kurdish uprisings have remained unknown. The burial places of Sheikh Said, Seyit Rıza, those who lost their lives in Geliyê Zilan and those who fell in the Ağrı Resistance remain unknown. Until the 1990s, our martyr comrades were also largely denied the right to be commemorated. For example, the whereabouts of the remains of comrade Egîd (Mahsum Korkmaz) are still unknown. The graves of all the comrades from that period remain unknown. This largely remained the case until 2000. As is known, there was a ceasefire between 2013 and 2015. During that period, we established many cemeteries for our martyr comrades in Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) and Southern Kurdistan (Başur), and brought our martyr comrades together there.


When the war resumed, our cemeteries were also targeted. This is well known; the public knows it, everyone knows it. In Garzan, they even exhumed the bones of our martyr comrades and took them to Kilyos in Istanbul. They want history to disappear; they want to leave us without a past. But now there is a peace process; this is a new period. If peace is to be established between the Kurdish people and the state, between Kurds, Turks and Arabs, if there is to be peace, then no one’s past should be suppressed in this way. For this reason, we want to bring all our martyr comrades together. This issue, extending back to those from the earliest periods, including Şêx Seîd, Seyit Rıza and Geliyê Zilan, must also be resolved within the framework of this peace and resolution process. We know the whereabouts of most of our martyr comrades, particularly those who lost their lives from 2000 to the present day. We need to bring them all together. As for those whose names were recently announced, their families can rest assured that the remains of most of them, with perhaps only a few exceptions, are under our control.


We attach great importance to this issue. We are currently bringing them together and want to gather them all in cemeteries for our martyr comrades. We are working on this issue. We will not allow any of our martyr comrades to be lost. We are doing everything we can, and of course, we also ask for the assistance of those who have information. We want to bring all our martyr comrades together. They are the values and the history of this people. Their memory must belong to their society; they must not be lost. They must never be forgotten. This is how we must honour and protect the memory of our martyr comrades. As a people, we must embrace their legacy. We are the comrades of these friends; we live for them. The meaning of our lives is to fulfil their aspirations. Therefore, our priority is undoubtedly to safeguard the remains of our comrades and ensure that their memory becomes part of history. We are focusing on this issue; it is on our agenda. In brief, that is the situation.


There are calls for a national day of mourning. What would you like to say about these calls?


It is true that our people and our families are mourning and holding condolence gatherings. But from our perspective and in our approach, this is not mourning in the conventional, sombre sense. We mourn, but ours is a different …

title: Sultan Kara was not protected despite seeking help
content:
Three women have been killed and three others have died under suspicious circumstances in Diyarbakır (Amed) in the first eight months of this year. The city has now witnessed another femicide. On the evening of 26 August, Ersan Akdemir shot and killed 32-year-old Sultan Akdemir (Kara), from whom he was in the process of divorcing. Sultan Kara, who married four years ago, prepared a divorce petition two months ago in order to end the marriage. After deciding to divorce, she moved in with her sister. Kara was killed in Sümerpark in the Yenişehir district, where Akdemir had gone on the pretext of seeing their child. The perpetrator fled after taking the child from Fatma’s arms and has still not been apprehended. Şehriban Kara, the sister of Fatma Kara, spoke about the killing and said that Sultan had been subjected to systematic violence and death threats. She called for the perpetrator to be apprehended as soon as possible.


She filed for divorce two months ago


Sultan Kara was critically wounded at the scene and later died at the hospital where she was taken. She was laid to rest in Yeniköy Cemetery in the city centre. Kara was reported to have said after separating from the perpetrator, “I am very happy and at peace. I am free of him.” Sultan Kara had been subjected to violence throughout her marriage. On one occasion, she went to a police station seeking help but was reportedly sent away with the words, “Go to your own family’s home.” It also emerged that the perpetrator’s family repeatedly threatened her to prevent her from filing a complaint and that her daughter was taken away from her during this period as a means of intimidation.


Şehriban Kara summed up what happened to her sister with the words, “No one did anything.” Kara said, “My sister is dead, and we are all devastated,” adding that the perpetrator had also displayed similar behaviour in a previous marriage. She continued: “The state does nothing. Our sister is dead. She had been married for four years, and every morning my sister would say, ‘He is going to kill me.’ Twice, he beat her almost to death. He threatened her and assaulted her. Even when she was pregnant, he put his hands around her throat and tried to kill her.”


He threatened her every day


Şehriban Kara said: “His family threatened her so that she would not file a complaint. She filed a divorce petition two months ago and would say, ‘I am very happy, I am at peace. I am free of him.’ Along with the divorce petition, she had also requested a restraining order. After she decided to divorce him, the perpetrator threatened both my older sister and Sultan with death. My sister is dead, while that man is still walking around freely. Women are being killed and no one is taking this seriously. I want justice. Enough is enough!”

author: DebConf 25
title: Preseed your PBX for Fun and Profit
content:
by Chris Maj


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/147-preseed-your-pbx-for-fun-and-profit/


What is a PBX ?


Private Branch eXchange (PBX) systems connect desk phones in your school or office to outside lines from the telephone company. Over the past 25 years,

open source Asterisk-based systems like FreePBX

 replaced many proprietary competitors in phone closets around the world, by bridging calls between legacy analog copper lines, digital interfaces such as ISDN PRIs, and now ubiquitous Voice-over-IP (VoIP) solutions like SIP and WebRTC.


Why call a PBX an embedded application ?


PBX systems typically run around the clock, routing low latency audio streams and providing emergency calling capabilities to end users. Sangoma produces a line of hardware appliances, as well as cloud solutions, that offer curated FreePBX web interface experiences to help non-Linux users manage their systems effectively.


When did Sangoma start using Debian ?


For many years, Sangoma targeted CentOS for installations; but when the CentOS EOL date of July 2024 came up on the horizon, the decision was made to switch to Debian as the primary target for new FreePBX deployments. This overhaul involved migrating internal build pipelines and many pieces of custom code, including our ISO delivery mechanism.


Where is this talk going ?


During construction of the new FreePBX 17 Distro ISO, derived from Debian 12, we endeavored to make the install

as simple as possible

 using both existing

and potentially novel

 preseed customization ideas. Highlights of this talk will include:


Presentation of our GPLv2'd

Ansible role "

sngfd12

"

 for quickly generating a custom preseeded ISO based on the upstream stock Debian ISO as input.


Controlling expression of preseed selection at GRUB installer prompt using a unique

"spice level"

 concept.


Automatically partitioning, RAIDing, and resizing (sharing some clever insights

for partman fans

 😃


Novel approaches to

randomized password generation

 during installation - a topic particularly relevant to embedded application developers w/r/t ongoing regulatory changes in this area.

author: DebConf 25
title: The Role of Free Software and Debian in Green Sustainability
content:
by Mylena  Angelica


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/63-the-role-of-free-software-and-debian-in-green-sustainability/


This talk explores the pivotal role of free software, with a focus on Debian, in advancing sustainability within the technology sector. As digital infrastructures continue to grow, the environmental footprint of proprietary software becomes increasingly apparent. In this session, we will discuss how free software reduces the ecological impact of proprietary alternatives by promoting energy-efficient practices, longevity, and reuse. Debian, as an open-source project, not only minimizes the need for frequent hardware upgrades but also encourages more sustainable development practices in software creation and distribution.


The audience for this talk includes developers, open-source enthusiasts, and environmental advocates interested in understanding how technology can contribute to environmental sustainability. Attendees will gain insight into how Debian’s open-source philosophy aligns with green computing principles, helping reduce electronic waste and supporting long-term environmental goals. Key topics will include the advantages of using lightweight software, optimizing resource consumption, and how the community-driven nature of Debian fosters a culture of sustainability.

author: Sandra de Castro
title: Os leitores e suas estantes
content:
Os japoneses criaram uma palavra pra designar a prática de acumular livros:

Tsundoku

. Algo como

tsun-

empilhar e

doku-

leitura

.

 Pra ter gerado um conceito específico, a prática não deve ser incomum por lá, o que maculou um pouco meu estereótipo de estimação sobre a moderação do mundo oriental.


Prática talvez não seja a melhor palavra, parece estar mais na esfera da mania, vício, falta de noção de realidade e tempo de vida. Os

tsundokuers


(

o anglicismo é por minha conta) vão, ao longo do tempo, erguendo suas bibliotecas. Porém, a consequência de ser este tipo de empilhador é erguer, em paralelo, uma antibiblioteca: um conjunto de tudo o que ainda não leu, quem sabe jamais lerá. Não parece uma coisa muito boa, mas fazer parte da categoria dos que só criam antibiblioteca, é pior. Estes, sequer apelido japonês têm.


Também existem os bibliófilos, esses com raiz grega biblio = livro. Têm livros raros, edições únicas, várias traduções dos mesmos textos. Humberto Eco tinha uns 30.000 livros e, pelo que se sabe, era desprovido de antibiblioteca. Tenho pra mim que um

tsundokuer

 gera muito mais empatia do que um bibliófilo.


Uma antibiblioteca é sempre motivo de angústia. Inclusive quanto à sua disposição nas estantes. Talvez alguns os organizem colocando todos os livros nunca lidos em prateleiras específicas, ou camuflem o acervo, misturando-os aos livros lidos, impressionando visitas e apaziguando um pouco sua mente devedora.


Pra você que lê isso e, em pânico, começa a caçar na sua estante tudo o que comprou e sequer tirou do plástico, calma. Lendo Irene Vallejo, autora de

O infinito em um junco

 (que comprei e li!), minha porção livreira nipônica foi acolhida. Ter uma porção de livros não lidos é sinal de otimismo, esperança na vida. É a crença materializada de que há um futuro você e que esse você do futuro um dia lerá tudo aquilo. O livro que você comprou hoje é uma aposta no amanhã. Bom, né?


Mas e quando você descobre, como eu, que além da biblioteca e antibiblioteca, você tem biblioteca ectoplásmica, composta por todos os livros que leu, despossuída de si mesma? Funciona assim: encontro um determinado livro na estante e penso: caramba, eu tinha esse livro, nem sabia, vou ler! Abro e vejo rabiscos, comentários, trechos sublinhados. A primeira reação é a indignação: quem se atreveu a rabiscar meu livro? A segunda, mais lúcida, percebe os indícios: garranchos no estilo único da minha letra feia; sublinhados no estilo inconfundível de um eletroencefalograma. Sim, fui eu. Li fora do corpo, não restando sequer um traço de memória sobre aquilo.


Alguns me dizem:

ah, teu cérebro não gravou porque você não se interessava pelo assunto?

 Elas não me compreendem. As reflexões, as anotações, os diálogos que travei com o autor, tudo mostra que sim, me interessava e muito. O que me faz concluir que alguns cérebros vêm com o

software

 que junta interesse + armazenamento. A memória então fica lá, salva e resgatável. No entanto, há os que vieram com o

software

, porém jamais atualizaram sua versão. Estes quase se equiparam à minha categoria, a de muitas (muitas) leituras fantasmagóricas.


Talvez deva adotar a estratégia de um amigo, também praticante de leitura incorpórea. Ele foca no momento, lê e não se frustra, apenas desfruta. Tipo

mindfulness.

 Já outra amiga, leitora desde que circulava pelo mundo só usando Pampers, tem a capacidade de citar de memória trechos inteiros. Nossa amizade sólida me salva das retaliações pela minha inveja explícita.


Tento aprender a conviver com isso, mas ainda tenho o péssimo costume de prometer a mim mesma as releituras. Assim, todos os que foram lidos — biblioteca, mais os que estão por ler — antibiblioteca, mais os livros ectoplásmicos, somam-se às releituras que nunca farei.


Me resta arrumar minha estante, colocando todos os livros misturados, dando volume, porque, sabe, isso sempre impressiona as visitas.

author: Taha Rezaei
title: Enchentes no Nepal e Tibete mostram que recuperação de desastres anteriores é crucial
content:
As inundações repentinas na fronteira entre Nepal e Tibete destruíram casas, estradas, pontes e projetos locais de geração de energia hidrelétrica. A inundação do rio Bhote Koshi está afetando 50 mil moradores. Mais de 500 pessoas morreram, e centenas estão desaparecidas, incluindo turistas estrangeiros.


Essa região do Himalaia ainda não havia se recuperado das inundações do rio Bhote Koshi em 2025, que mataram nove pessoas ao arrastar uma “ponte da amizade”

que ligava o Nepal à China

, interrompendo o comércio e o transporte por meses.


No Sri Lanka, as recentes inundações e deslizamentos de terra atingiram comunidades que ainda estavam se recuperando do ciclone Ditwah, que havia causado danos generalizados há nove meses.

Com pouco tempo

 para se recuperar do ciclone, as

comunidades

 ficaram sem proteção contra novas inundações. Mais de 15 mil pessoas foram diretamente afetadas e

6.800 pessoas

 foram deslocadas em agosto deste ano.


A

gestão do risco de desastres

 geralmente considera a intensidade da próxima inundação, incêndio florestal, ciclone ou seca. Mas os exemplos do Nepal e do Sri Lanka mostram duas dimensões que costumam ser negligenciadas:

quão rapidamente uma comunidade consegue

se recuperar

 e se isso acontecerá antes da chegada do próximo desastre.


Raramente um desastre deixa um lugar exatamente como ele era antes. E quando um segundo desastre acontece, estradas e pontes ainda podem estar danificadas, enquanto famílias já podem ter gastado suas economias. Empresas ainda podem estar em dificuldades. Governos podem continuar financiando a reconstrução, enquanto hospitais e outros serviços públicos permanecem sob pressão.


Se outro evento extremo ocorrer antes que esses sistemas tenham se recuperado, ele não encontrará a mesma comunidade que existia antes do primeiro desastre.

Encontrará um lugar com menor resiliência e

infraestrutura enfraquecida

.


Povoado no centro-norte do Nepal soterrado após inundações na fronteira com o Tibete


Uma maneira útil de compreender esse fenômeno é entender o chamado “intervalo de recuperação” (

recovery gap,

 em inglês): a relação entre o tempo necessário para a recuperação antes de outro

desastre capaz de causar danos

.


Imagine duas comunidades que passam por inundações semelhantes. Em uma delas, o último grande desastre ocorreu há dez anos. As casas foram reconstruídas, a infraestrutura foi reparada e os recursos de emergência foram repostos.


Na outra, o desastre mais recente aconteceu há seis meses. As estradas continuam em reconstrução, as famílias ainda estão deslocadas ou endividadas, e as autoridades públicas continuam pagando pela reconstrução. A nova inundação pode ser fisicamente semelhante nos dois locais. Suas consequências, porém, podem não ser.


Uma recuperação incompleta pode aumentar substancialmente as perdas no longo prazo.

 Um estudo de 2025 sobre inundações recorrentes nas Filipinas constatou que as perdas causadas por estas tragédias aumentaram

40% entre 2000 e 2018

 devido à recuperação incompleta.


Isso sugere que as perdas provocadas por desastres recorrentes nem sempre são simplesmente cumulativas.

O primeiro desastre pode alterar as condições em que o segundo desastre ocorre, fazendo com que os efeitos das tragédias subsequentes sejam muito mais graves.


A recuperação tem tempos diferentes


A recuperação costuma ser descrita como algo binário, como se uma comunidade conseguisse ou não se reerguer. Na realidade, trata-se mais de uma escala gradual.


O fornecimento de eletricidade e água potável pode ser restabelecido em poucos dias. Mas uma estrada danificada pode levar meses para ser reparada. A reconstrução de moradias pode levar anos. Empresas podem reabrir, enquanto ainda carregam dívidas substanciais.


As finanças das famílias, os ecossistemas e o bem-estar psicológico podem se recuperar em escalas de tempo completamente diferentes.


Assim, um lugar pode parecer recuperado de acordo com um indicador, mas continuar altamente vulnerável

de acordo com outro

.


Foram necessários mais de dez anos para que Nova Orleans, nos Estados Unidos, conseguisse se recuperar significativamente após o

furacão Katrina, em 2005

. Embora as operações básicas de emergência e o restabelecimento de energia tenham levado de semanas a meses, a reconstrução completa dos bairros, a estabilização da população e grandes melhorias no sistema de proteção contra inundações se estenderam por 15 anos ou mais. E isso em um dos …

title: Gülistan Doku soruşturmasında 5'inci dalga operasyonu 10 kişi gözaltına alındı
content:
Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek Gülistan Doku’nun kaybolmasına ilişkin yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında bugün 5'inci dalga operasyon gerçekleştirildiğini ve 10 kişinin gözaltına alındığını bildirdi.

Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, X hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda şunları kaydetti:

"Adalet ve İçişleri Bakanlıklarımızın güçlü koordinasyonu; Cumhuriyet Başsavcılıklarımız ile Emniyet ve Jandarma teşkilatlarımızın etkin iş birliğiyle faili meçhul suçları aydınlatmaya devam ediyoruz. Güncel teknolojik imkanlar ve elde edilen yeni deliller ışığında bugün iki önemli dosyada daha kritik gelişmelere ulaştık.

Gülistan Doku'nun kaybolmasına ilişkin Erzurum ve Tunceli Cumhuriyet Başsavcılıklarımız ile Emniyet ve Jandarma teşkilatlarımızın koordinasyonunda yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında bugün 5. dalga operasyon gerçekleştirildi ve 10 şüpheli gözaltına alındı. Soruşturmada, Gülistan'ın son görüldüğü köprü ve zaman dilimine ilişkin PTS ve iletişim kayıtlarında yeni bulgulara, kaybolmasının ardından Doku'nun Instagram hesabına gerçekleştirilen şüpheli erişim/işlemlere ve su altı arama çalışmalarına ilişkin dikkat çekici tespitlere ulaşıldı. Adli makamlardan gizlendiği belirlenen dalgıç defterindeki kayıtlarla resmi arama tutanaklarının uyuşmadığı tespit edildi. Gülistan'a ait bazı kişisel eşyaların, intihar ihtimalini destekleyen bir görüntü oluşturmak amacıyla su altına sonradan yerleştirilmiş olabileceğine ilişkin bulgulara ulaşıldı."

Gürlek ayrıca Dede Baltacı cinayeti dosyası kapsamında beş şüpheli tespit edildiğini belirterek; "İkinci önemli gelişme ise 18 yıldır faili belirlenemeyen Dede Baltacı cinayetinde yaşandı. 2008 yılında Şereflikoçhisar'da ölü bulunan Baltacı'nın dosyası, Faili Meçhul Suçları Araştırma Daire Başkanlığımızın koordinasyonunda Şereflikoçhisar Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığımız ve Şereflikoçhisar İlçe Jandarma Komutanlığımızın yürüttüğü çalışmalarla yeniden incelendi. Daraltılmış baz çalışması, HTS kayıtları, Adli Tıp raporu ve bu verilerle uyumlu tanık beyanı sonucunda cinayetin failleri olduğu değerlendirilen 5 şüpheli tespit edildi. Gerçekleştirilen operasyonun ardından F.K., R.K., A.Ö. ve F.E. tutuklandı" dedi.

author: Unknown
title: Ekvador'da eski Devlet Başkanı Moreno'ya rüşvetten 5 yıl hapis
content:
Fotoğraf: Agencia de Noticias ANDES/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 2.0

Ekvador’da eski Devlet Başkanı Lenin Moreno, ülkenin en büyük hidroelektrik santrali Coca Codo Sinclair’in inşasıyla bağlantılı yolsuzluk davasında suçlu bulundu. Mahkeme, 73 yaşındaki Moreno’yu Çinli Sinohydro şirketinden rüşvet almak suçundan 5 yıl hapis cezasına mahkum etti.

Mahkeme heyeti, yürüme engeli bulunan Moreno’nun cezasını cezaevinde değil, ev hapsinde çekmesine karar verdi. Mahkeme ayrıca eski Devlet Başkanı’nın kamu görevlerinden sürekli olarak men edilmesine hükmetti.

Moreno’nun fiziksel engeli nedeniyle cezaevine gönderilmeyeceği belirtildi.

Dava kapsamında Moreno’nun eşi, kızı, iki kardeşi ve diğer bazı aile üyeleri de suçlu bulundu.

Mahkeme, Moreno’nun eşi ve kızını 2 yıl 6 ay hapis cezasına çarptırdı. Aile üyelerinin de rüşvet ağına dahil olduğu sonucuna varıldı.

Ekvador’un en büyük hidroelektrik santrali olan Coca Codo Sinclair’in inşası, ülkede uzun süredir devam eden yolsuzluk tartışmalarının merkezinde yer alıyordu.

Çinli Sinohydro şirketine verilen milyarlarca dolarlık proje kapsamında rüşvet ödemeleri yapıldığı iddiaları uzun süredir soruşturuluyordu. Mahkeme, söz konusu ödemelerin Moreno’nun Devlet Başkanlığı döneminde gerçekleştiğini ve Moreno’nun rüşvet sürecinde aktif rol aldığını tespit etti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: DebConf 25
title: Mitigating kernel development bottlenecks and supporting the GNU/Linux ecosystem with kworkflow
content:
by David Tadokoro


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/62-mitigating-kernel-development-bottlenecks-and-supporting-the-gnulinux-ecosystem-with-kworkflow/


The Linux kernel project sits at the base of a gigantic and complex Free Software ecosystem. As a two-way road, downstream projects - the most prominent, Debian - feed off the kernel development while returning contributions to the upstream and giving it importance. Be it downstream or upstream development, if you work with the Linux kernel source code, chances are that you probably had to do one (if not all) of the following: set up a testing environment for custom kernels; fetching, optimizing, and managing several .config files; building a kernel from source; deploying a custom kernel to a testing environment. Before doing these tasks, some questions must be answered: Do I use physical machines or VMs as testing environments? What will the distro(s) of the target machine(s) be? Where do I get a base .config for a specific distro and architecture? What optimizations to do for building? How do I deploy the custom kernel to a particular testing environment?


For each combination of answers to these questions, surely, there will be a different sequence of commands, processes, paths to consider, and so on. After a few runs, you will probably be tired of manually doing all this work and will create scripts to automate your workflow. The problem is, if your workflow mutates a little or has slight variations, or your scripts have bugs, you will need to waste your precious development time maintaining these scripts that were not your objective in the first place! This is where

kworkflow

 (kw), a

Developer Automation Workflow System

 (DAWS), enters the scene. With a unified interface to many commands, kw abstracts many of these details, streamlines and automates time-consuming workflows, and enforces good practices so kernel developers can focus on the code they are writing, not on whether the make command was typed correctly.


Want to up a VM? Run kw vm --up;


Want to fetch a .config from within a machine in the network? Run kw kernel-config-manager --fetch;


How about compiling with optimizations and cross-compilation? Do some simple configuration with kw config, then just fire kw build;


I doubt installing custom kernels and modules is as simple as running one command, right? Wrong, you just need kw deploy.


In reality, kw does much more than this. For example, there is a

Terminal User Interface

 (TUI) feature to consult and manipulate patches sent to the mailing lists, resulting from a PhD applied research. This talk will introduce the key features of kw and show how it can be used to improve your kernel development workflows.


Even though kernel development has worked well for more than 30 years, we understand bottlenecks in developers' workflows are risking the long-term sustainability of the whole ecosystem, and projects like kw are vital to avoid this scenario beyond just automating tasks. At the end of the talk, we will want to collect feedback from the best community in the GNU/Linux distro world, the Debian community, about what kw is doing right and wrong and how the community experience and knowledge can help us have a more comprehensive view of the GNU/Linux ecosystem.

author: Unknown
title: Yenidoğan Çetesi soruşturmasında adı geçen hastane 200 milyon liraya satışta
content:
İstanbul’da yürütülen Yenidoğan Çetesi soruşturması kapsamında yönetimi Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu’na (TMSF) devredilen sağlık kuruluşlarından Esenler Güney Hastanesi satışa çıkarıldı.

Soruşturma kapsamında çok sayıda hastane ve sağlık şirketine kayyum atanmış, bu kuruluşların bir bölümü TMSF yönetimine devredilmişti. Güney Hastanesi Sağlık Hizmetleri Ltd. Şti. bünyesinde faaliyet gösteren Esenler Güney Hastanesi de TMSF yönetimine devredilen kuruluşlar arasında yer aldı.

Soruşturma sürecinin ardından söz konusu hastanelerin ruhsatları iptal edilirken bazı sağlık kuruluşlarının satışına ilişkin işlemler de TMSF tarafından başlatıldı.

Daha önce Avcılar Hospital, Reyap İstanbul ve Reyap Çorlu hastaneleri için de satış ilanları yayımlanmıştı.

TMSF’nin yayımladığı ihale duyurusuna göre Güney Sağlık Hizmetleri Ltd. Şti. için 200 milyon lira muhammen bedel belirlendi.

İhaleye katılmak isteyenlerin idari ve mali belgelerini içeren kapalı zarfları 29 Eylül 2026 saat 16.00’a kadar Satış Komisyonu’na elden teslim etmesi gerekiyor. Bu tarihten sonra sunulacak teklifler değerlendirmeye alınmayacak.

İhale, 30 Eylül 2026 saat 11.00’de TMSF’nin İstanbul Esentepe’de bulunan binasında gerçekleştirilecek.

Kapalı zarfların açılmasıyla başlayacak süreçte sunulan teklifler doğrultusunda “Kısa Liste” oluşturulacak. Ardından açık artırma aşamasına geçilecek.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Unwavering, a mother of EJK victim confronts a decade of impunity
content:
The second truth-telling session of the Philippine Truth Commission hears the case of 17-year-old extrajudicial killing victim Darwin Hamoy and the search for justice of her mother, Mariza Hamoy on August 27, 2026. Photo by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

“It was easy for other people to tell me to give up the fight. But win or lose, I’ll never stop fighting. I’ll never lose hope for Darwin.”

MANILA – Mariza Hamoy, mother of extrajudicial killing victim Darwin Hamoy, has tried to go after the 16 police officers who killed her son. But her legal defeat has not deterred her search for justice, even once, even in the face of mounting threats.

“It was easy for other people to tell me to give up the fight. But win or lose, I’ll never stop fighting. I’ll never lose hope for Darwin,” she said in Filipino during the second truth-telling session of the Philippine Truth Commission, a civil society-led initiative to probe the “drug war” of Rodrigo Duterte, on Thursday, August 27.

Darwin and four of his friends were killed by the policemen in a buy-bust operation in Payatas, Quezon City, on August 15, 2016. He was 17 years old.

He was buying cigarettes for his friend William Bordios, also one of the victims, during a birthday celebration. It was the first “nanlaban” (drug suspect supposedly fought back) cases during the early years of Rodrigo Duterte’s anti-illegal drug campaign.

“My son was diligent, kind, and good at math…He was helping us work to sustain our family,” Hamoy said.

Hamoy was a street sweeper while her husband was a construction worker. Both were earning below the daily minimum wage then. “Our income was not enough. He [Darwin] was helping us buy rice and water for our daily needs,” she said.

When her son was killed, Hamoy did not immediately have access to his body. It took her eight days to find her son’s body in a funeral home in Quezon City. She was asked to pay P15,000 (US$240.72) to retrieve the remains. It took her a total of two weeks to get Darwin buried.

“I only had P2,000 (US$32.10) during that time. I told them if I could make a downpayment so I could bring Darwin home. I told them that I was a street sweeper. They refused,” Mariza recalled. “It was when I told them that I was contacting the media that they allowed me to make the downpayment. But they asked me for another P2,000 for his clothes to be used at the wake.”

Tearingly, she said that she could not afford to see Darwin for the last time with his old clothes. So she decided to buy a barong.

Hamoy filed two legal cases against the 16 police officers who came from the Quezon City Police District Station 6. A 2017 Reuters investigation revealed that 39 percent of the city’s killings from anti-drug operations can be attributed to the QCPD Station 6 police officers, who reportedly called themselves “Davao Boys” since they came from or near Davao.

The first case was filed through the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) in 2017, which was later endorsed to the Office of the Ombudsman for criminal charges. But a year later, the charges were dismissed because there was “no evidence that the police used excessive force,” according to former Executive Secretary Salvador Medialdea.

Philippine Truth Commission Chairperson Raul Pangalangan, who was also a former judge of the International Criminal Court (ICC), explained the use of excessive force. He said, “There were an overwhelming number of police, considering that the victims were unarmed.”

The second truth-telling session of the Philippine Truth Commission hears the case of 17-year-old extrajudicial killing victim Darwin Hamoy and the search for justice of her mother, Mariza Hamoy on August 27, 2026. Photos by Dominic Gutoman/Bulatlat

The second case was filed before the Philippine National Police Internal Affairs Service (PNP IAS) in 2017. A year after, the PNP IAS filed charges of grave misconduct and grave irregularity against the 16 policemen in 2018. It was only this year that Hamoy was informed that the charges were dismissed.

Their commander, Lito Patay, was also charged with two counts of grave neglect of duty and one count each of less grave neglect of duty and simple neglect of duty by the PNP IAS due to his leadership at the time of Hamoy’s death. But Malacañang cleared him of charges in 2022, when Duterte was still in power.

1943 :

 Les nazis dissolvent le gouvernement du Danemark occupé. En retour, les Danois-es coulent leur propre flotte militaire.

 Insurrection slovaque contre les nazis.

 En Angleterre, l'IRA place deux bombes à Solihull ainsi qu'une troisième dans les magasins Harrod à Londres.

author: DebConf 25
title: ci.rocm.debian.net: a Debian CI with AMD GPUs, for AI/ML packages
content:
by Christian Kastner


At: DebConf25


https://debconf25.debconf.org/talks/182-cirocmdebiannet-a-debian-ci-with-amd-gpus-for-aiml-packages/


Much of number-crunching today is performed on GPUs. This especially applies to AI/ML-driven workloads. ROCm is AMD's open source software stack for general purpose GPU computing, challenging Nvidia's CUDA.


The Debian ROCm team's mission is to integrate and support ROCm on Debian to the point that using an AMD GPU (enterprise and consumer) for computation tasks is only an apt-get away. And with "support", we don't just mean packaging the libraries: we want to actually demonstrate just how well ROCm works.


To this end, we forked Debian's CI tools and bootstrapped our own environment with GPU support, currently featuring more than a dozen GPU architectures.

Our CI

 works exactly like Debian's

official CI

, except that we only look at the subset of packages linked to ROCm libraries.


In this talk, I'll present a brief overview of our CI, and the policy and technical challenges we faced bootstrapping it. I'll then show how contributors can adapt their packages to get coverage in our CI.
